note: Raw results of the 2026-11-10 mobile UX review workflow (line numbers are as of that day and drift as the code changes). Summary: docs/mobile-ux/review.md. Plan: docs/mobile-ux/fix-plan.md.

system.area: Global design system (web/src/app.css tokens and classes) and Home Screen web app plumbing (app.html, static/manifest.webmanifest, routes/+layout.svelte), plus a global inventory of interactive selectors under 44px or under 14px across web/src. Device math: iPhone 15 Pro at 460ppi ÷ DPR 3 = 6.04 CSS px per mm, so 44px = 7.3mm. Research anchors: Apple HIG 44pt; WCAG 2.5.8 24px (AA) and 2.5.5 44px (AAA); Parhi et al. 9.2mm for single taps and 9.6mm for repeated thumb taps (≈56-58px); Hoober allows targets as close as 7mm centre-to-centre mid-screen (≈42px) and 10-12mm at the top and bottom edges (≈60-72px). Chess.com's Game Analysis puts its back/forward arrows in a bottom bar (support.chess.com/en/articles/10473022). The screenshots match the CSS math within about 1px: chips at 512-547, Play at 556-593, move buttons 30px tall, foot buttons at 760-803.

issues.title: No hit-area or spacing primitive: 24 phone-visible controls are under 44px, the tightest on the drill's most-tapped row
issues.where: app.css:122-215 (only .btn, .icon-btn and .input reach 44px); local overrides at drill:1408-1412, 1440-1461, 1415-1429, 1321-1351, 2138-2141; explore:309-320; leaks:113-116
issues.evidence: The worst row is the drill navrow (y 556-594). Moves are 4 + 21.75 + 4 = 29.75px tall (4.9mm at 6.04 px/mm) with 1px gaps (drill:1445, 0.2mm). The arrows are overridden from 44 to 34×34 (drill:1410) and sit 2px from the move scroller (drill:1404). Play is 38px tall and 2 + 4 = 6px from Next. The chips are 36px with 5px gaps (drill:1325). Parhi et al. recommend 9.6mm (≈58px) for repeated thumb taps, and Hoober puts the closest workable spacing at 7mm (≈42px) centre-to-centre even mid-screen; short moves like 'd5' are 30px wide, a 31px pitch. Nothing in app.css limits how small a component can make a target or its gap; the gaps in use are 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6px. Of the 24 sub-44px selectors in elements[], 9 are under 24px.
issues.fix: Add to app.css: `:root { --tap: 44px; --tap-gap: 8px }` and a utility that grows the touch box into empty space without moving anything: `.hit { position: relative } .hit::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: min(0px, calc((100% - var(--tap)) / 2)) 0 }`. Rule: distinct targets stay at least var(--tap-gap) apart. Caveat: inside overflow:auto rows (.moves, .chips) the ::after gets clipped, so there make the items fill the row instead. `.moves, .mv { align-self: stretch }` makes moves 38px tall at no layout cost, because Play already makes the row 38px. Use the same 38px for the arrows, at 40px wide. Space budget for 44px chips and arrows: dropping the foot-row (28px + 8px gap) by moving the streak to the top bar and ⋯ into the Why sheet frees 36px. A chess.com-style option: a full-width .toolbar primitive with equal-width buttons at least 48px tall for ‹ ›, Play and Why.
issues.impact: On every card, stepping through moves and picking lines takes fingertip precision, and missing by 1px hits the neighbouring move. This matches the user's main complaint.

issues.title: Touch feedback is desktop-first: iOS tap highlight removed, :active on only 2 classes, 14 :hover rules stick after a tap
issues.where: app.css:64 (-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent); app.css:137 (.btn:active); +page.svelte:316 (.drill-cta:active); :hover at app.css:166, drill:1367,1466,1778,1904, +page:425, lines:210-211, explore:322-323,387, settings:292, LeakCard:81
issues.evidence: With the highlight transparent, chips, moves, arrows, Play, segmented buttons, the tab bar, ⋯ and text links show nothing when touched. WebKit applies :active only if a touch listener exists (bug 138816, re-verified on iOS 17.6.1 and still open in 2026). Today one exists only by accident: Board.svelte:97-98 adds window/document touchstart listeners, so even .btn:active never fires on Settings, Lines, or Home without leak cards. Meanwhile :hover stays on after a tap until the next tap elsewhere: IMG_1383 shows a grey pill left on the › arrow. drill:1467-1471 gives `button.mv:hover` the same style as `.mv.current`, so a stale hover looks like a second current move.
issues.fix: Wrap every :hover rule in `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) { … }`. In +layout.svelte onMount add `document.addEventListener('touchstart', () => {}, { passive: true })`, or put `ontouchstart=""` on <body> in app.html. Add a shared pressed state in app.css: `:where(.icon-btn, .chip, .chip-line, .mv, .play, .segmented button, .text-btn, .tabbar a, summary):active { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--text) 12%, transparent); transition-duration: 0ms }`.
issues.impact: Users can't see which of two adjacent small targets is under their thumb until the action fires. Stale highlights look like toggled states.

issues.title: Inputs are 15px, so iOS zooms on focus, and the zoom persists across the whole SPA
issues.where: app.css:62 (body 15px), app.css:91-95 (input font: inherit), app.css:217-226 (.input has no font-size); inputs at +page.svelte:68, settings:109, settings:157
issues.evidence: iOS Safari zooms into any input under 16px on focus and stays zoomed after blur. The app is a client-side SPA (+layout.ts ssr=false), so the zoom carries over to /drill: the 381px board no longer fits the screen width. WebKit's fast-tap rule (no click delay, no double-tap zoom) only applies at initial scale (webkit.org/blog/5610), so after that, taps are delayed and quick repeat taps can zoom further until the user pinches out.
issues.fix: `.input { font-size: 16px; }` (or `max(16px, 1em)`). Don't use maximum-scale=1 instead: it blocks pinch zoom on Android.
issues.impact: Rarely triggered (account and token fields), but afterwards the drill is cropped and sluggish until the user notices and pinches out.

issues.title: No touch-action: manipulation anywhere, so quick repeat taps on arrows and moves can double-tap-zoom
issues.evidence: The only touch-action rules are on the board (none, Board.svelte:121), the sheet rows (none, drill:2081-2084) and the sheet chips (pan-x, drill:2087). The › arrow and the moves get tapped 2-3 times in a row. WebKit only suppresses double-tap for device-width pages at initial scale, and buttons zooming on double-tap is still reported with a correct viewport (piccalil.li, Sept 2026). touch-action: manipulation disables double-tap at every zoom level and keeps pinch zoom.
issues.fix: In app.css: `:where(a, button, summary, label, input, select, textarea, [role='button']) { touch-action: manipulation; }`. It has to go on the controls themselves: touch-action only intersects up to the nearest scroll container, so a rule on html wouldn't reach buttons inside .moves or .chips.
issues.impact: Mainly insurance, but cheap, and it closes the zoom chain from global-3.

issues.title: --text-3 'faint' is 3.95:1 and is used on tappable text
issues.where: app.css:9 (--text-3 #6b7180), app.css:44 (light #8b909a); used by .mv.past (drill:1463-1465), tab labels (+layout:169), ⋯ (drill:1896), .engine-toggle (drill:2058), home 'All' links (+page:165), .count (drill:1276-1280)
issues.evidence: Computed ratios: 3.95:1 on --bg, 3.67:1 on --bg-elev (the sheet), 3.38:1 on --bg-elev-2. The light theme is 2.96:1. WCAG 1.4.3 requires 4.5:1 for text at these sizes (11-15px). Earlier game moves in the move row and the 12px Engine-line toggle are tappable text in this colour, so users squint at small targets.
issues.fix: `--text-3: #838a99` gives 5.57 / 5.17 / 4.76:1 and still reads clearly dimmer than --text-2 (8.1:1). Light theme: `--text-3: #686d77` (4.80 / 5.19:1).

issues.title: Target edges are nearly invisible, so people aim at the label instead of the whole hit area
issues.where: app.css:151-154 (.btn-quiet fill), app.css:205 (.chip border), app.css:179, 195-199 (.segmented), drill:1408-1412 (arrows have no fill), drill:1891-1899 (⋯)
issues.evidence: Fill or border against the background: .btn-quiet 1.17:1, .chip border 1.34:1, .segmented track 1.17:1, the pressed segment against the track 1.09:1, .mv.current 1.17:1. The step arrows and ⋯ have no shape at rest, so what the user sees is an 18px glyph inside a 34×34 or ≈34×28 box. Targets look smaller than they are, and that invites precise aiming.
issues.fix: Add `--line-strong: #4a505c` (2.4:1) for interactive outlines: `.btn-quiet, .chip { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--line-strong) }`. Make the pressed segment accent-tinted, like `.chip[aria-pressed]`, instead of --bg-elev. Give the step arrows a visible pill or circle as big as their hit area, the way Chess.com draws its bottom-bar ‹ › buttons.

issues.title: ⋯ menu: a small trigger right above Continue opens a 'stop drilling' action with no undo
issues.evidence: The summary is ≈34×28 (padding 0 8px, line-height 28px) at y 724-752, 8px above the right half of Continue (760-804), right where a right thumb lands. A <details> menu doesn't close when you tap outside it. The item is unpadded 14px text, and one tap calls suspendCard() permanently. Nothing un-suspends a card; the only way back is Settings → Reset drill progress, which deletes every card (resetCards).
issues.fix: Build one shared bottom action-sheet component: rows at least 48px tall, closes on a backdrop tap, has a Cancel row. After suspending, show a 5-second toast 'Stopped drilling Bc4 · Undo'. Add a 'Suspended cards' list with restore in Settings (this needs a new unsuspendCard API). Move the trigger out of the foot, for example into the Why sheet header.

issues.title: The one-screen fit is coincidental (about 2px to spare); any overflow scrolls the app under the status bar
issues.evidence: Phone column: 63 (safe-t + 4) + 36 bar + 6 + 14 eval + 4 + 381 board + 8 + 36 chips + 8 + 38 navrow + 8 + 42 note + 16 + 42.3 result box (1 line) + 12 + 136 foot (10+28+8+44+46) = 850.3 of 852. A 2-line result box (+20.3) or a 3-line note (+19.6) overflows. IMG_1390 and the 5:02 PM screenshot show the page scrolled with the top bar under the clock. The board is touch-action:none and covers 45% of the screen, so scrolling back is awkward.
issues.fix: On phones, build the drill as a fixed-height column: `main.focus { height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden; display: flex; flex-direction: column }`; `.drill, .stage, .panel { flex: 1; min-height: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column }`; give the note and result-box region `min-height: 0; overflow: hidden` and cap it at 2 lines, with the rest in Why?; `.foot { margin-top: auto; position: static }`. The board keeps its full width; only text gives way. Also add a status-bar scrim: `body::before { content: ''; position: fixed; inset: 0 0 auto; height: var(--safe-t); background: var(--bg); z-index: 45; pointer-events: none }`.

issues.title: The whole app rubber-bands, and the move and chip rows re-centre after every tap, so targets shift under the thumb
issues.where: app.css:318-323 (overscroll is set only while the sheet is open); drill/+page.svelte:735-749 (smooth scrollTo to centre), 1322-1328, 1440-1449
issues.evidence: There's no overscroll-behavior on html or body, so a slightly diagonal swipe on .chips or .moves drags the whole standalone app, top bar and Continue included. After each tap, an $effect smooth-scrolls the row to centre the current or selected item. The move area is ≈223px wide (x 42-265 in IMG_1389), so it can shift up to ≈112px while the thumb is heading for the next move.
issues.fix: `@media (display-mode: standalone) { html, body { overscroll-behavior: none } }` (supported since iOS 16), and `.chips, .moves, .sheet-lines { overscroll-behavior-x: contain }`. Only scroll a row when the current item is out of view: `el.scrollIntoView({ inline: 'nearest', block: 'nearest', behavior: 'smooth' })` with about 24px of scroll-padding.

issues.title: Inline text actions are 17-23px tall, and there's no global .text-btn
issues.where: drill:1072 'show it' (.seek .text-btn 1531-1538); drill:1007 'Back to the position' (1841-1845); drill:1168-1175 .engine-toggle (2054-2067); drill:1201-1208 .sources a (1822-1839); settings:153 (313-318), 161; lines:48; +page:165, 186; AnalysisStatus:41, 44; InstallHint:25 (44-49)
issues.evidence: 14px × 1.45 = 20.3px tall. 'show it' is ≈46×20 and sits inside the coloured result box every time a 'Good move' needs the taught move. The engine toggle is 2 + 17.4 + 2 + 2 = 23.4px, under the 24px WCAG 2.5.8 minimum, and drawn in 12px --text-3. Source links are 12px, so 17.4px tall, and the last one is cut off by the ellipsis. .text-btn is defined twice, at drill:1841 and settings:313. WCAG 2.5.8 exempts links inside sentences, but a thumb still has to hit them.
issues.fix: Define one global class: `.text-btn { position: relative; font-size: 15px; color: var(--accent) } .text-btn::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -12px -6px }`, which grows the hit area without changing line layout. On phones, put actions in buttons rather than sentences: while seeking, show 'Show it' as the foot's left .btn in place of 'Try again'. Make the engine toggle a 36-44px segmented control or a row in the sheet.

issues.title: .segmented buttons are 32px inside a 38px pill (a 3px dead ring), and .chip is 34px
issues.evidence: 32px is 5.3mm. The 3px container padding (app.css:177) looks tappable but does nothing, and segments are 2px apart. These are used for the five Settings toggles and the Lines and Leaks colour filters.
issues.fix: `.segmented button { height: 38px }` with the existing 3px padding gives a 44px control (or use `min-height: 44px` on the container and stretch the buttons). Use `.chip { height: 40px }` plus the .hit utility to reach 44px.

issues.title: Settings' two-tap destructive buttons never disarm, and they're 34px tall
issues.evidence: After one tap, confirmReset or confirmClear stays true until the page unmounts, so a stray tap minutes later wipes all drill progress or every stored game. The buttons are 6 + 21.75 + 6 = 33.75px tall with no side padding.
issues.fix: Disarm after about 4 seconds (`setTimeout(() => (confirmReset = false), 4000)`), give the armed state a filled red style, and set `.danger { min-height: 44px; padding: 0 12px }`.

issues.title: No type scale; controls and key status text use 12-13px
issues.where: app.css has no size tokens; drill:2177-2179 (streak 12px on phones), drill:2059 (engine toggle 12px), drill:1396 (.chip-line .ev 12px), drill:1547 (13px), explore:247-284, LeakCard:100-157
issues.evidence: Sizes in use: 9.5, 10, 10.5, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 22, 26, 28 and 30px. On phones the streak line ('2 in a row · 1 more…') drops to 12px.
issues.fix: Add tokens: `--fs-caption: 12px` (non-tappable text only), `--fs-small: 13px`, `--fs-body: 15px`, `--fs-title: 17px`, with the rule that tappable text is at least 15px.

issues.title: Long-press on link-styled controls opens the iOS link preview
issues.evidence: -webkit-touch-callout isn't set anywhere, so a resting or slow press on a tab or the X opens the iOS link preview instead of navigating. Only the board has user-select: none (Board.svelte:122).
issues.fix: `.tabbar a, a.icon-btn, a.btn, .drill-cta { -webkit-touch-callout: none; -webkit-user-select: none; user-select: none }`

issues.title: The expanded Why sheet puts Expand and Close top-right, 4px apart, with no swipe gesture
issues.evidence: Expanded, the sheet starts at 59 + 8 = 67, so the buttons sit at y 73-117, the hardest spot for a right thumb to reach. Two 44px buttons with different jobs are 4px apart (drill:1953). The head is touch-action:none, so the iOS-standard swipe down does nothing.
issues.fix: Add a grabber with drag down to collapse or close; the head already blocks page scrolling, so a drag won't conflict. Keep Expand and Close at least 8px apart, or merge them into one toggle.

issues.title: Landscape and side safe areas aren't handled, and iOS ignores the manifest orientation
issues.where: static/manifest.webmanifest (no orientation); app.css:31-32 (only top and bottom insets); app.css:65 (unprefixed text-size-adjust only)
issues.evidence: iOS doesn't support the manifest orientation member (firt.dev PWA notes). Rotated, the viewport is 852×393 but still matches max-width:899, so the board becomes 852 − 12 = 840px tall in a 393px-tall viewport, and content runs under the Dynamic Island side because there's no safe-area-inset-left/right.
issues.fix: Add `"orientation": "portrait"` to the manifest (Android honours it). For iOS, add `padding-inline: max(6px, env(safe-area-inset-left))` and a landscape layout for `(orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 500px)` with the board beside the panel. Add `-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%` next to the unprefixed rule.

issues.title: No :focus-visible styling
issues.evidence: Keyboard users (an iPad keyboard, or desktop with the drill's arrow and Esc shortcuts at drill:705-721) get only the browser's default focus rings, which look different in Safari and Chrome on these custom pill buttons.
issues.fix: `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px }`

strengths: .btn is 44px tall (app.css:127) and .icon-btn is 44×44 (app.css:159-160), the right baseline; .input is 46px (app.css:218).

The bottom tab bar gives five 78.6×58px targets above a 34px safe-area pad, primary navigation in the thumb zone. It's hidden during drills (+layout.svelte:206-208), so a tab can't be hit by accident mid-card.
viewport-fit=cover plus black-translucent, with --safe-t and --safe-b applied consistently (main, tab bar, foot, sheet). Continue's bottom edge (804) clears the home-indicator zone (818) by 14px.

The board uses touch-action:none and user-select:none (Board.svelte:121-122), so piece drags never scroll the page. Squares are 47.6px (381/8). Tapping the board to skip the intro and the sheet backdrop are big, forgiving targets.

The foot's action buttons are 44px tall with 10px gaps and flex widths of ≈100/100/160px, sticky in the natural thumb zone. End session is the only top-left control: a hard-to-reach corner suits a rare action.
Haptics on moves and results, including the iOS 18 switch-tick trick fired inside the touch (Board.svelte:45-67, haptics.ts), with a Test button in Settings.
Destructive Settings actions use a two-tap confirm, and .btn has a pressed scale (app.css:137-139).

Pinch zoom stays enabled (no user-scalable=no). prefers-reduced-motion is honoured app-wide (app.css:311-316). overflow-x: clip on html and body stops sideways wobble and keeps sticky working (app.css:66-67).
Contrast is high where it matters most: body text 16:1, --text-2 8.1:1, accent links 9.2:1, primary button label 9.2:1, result-box text 6.3-6.6:1.
InstallHint detects standalone mode correctly and explains Safari's 7-day storage eviction; theme-color is set for both colour schemes.

drill-sheet.area: Phone Why sheet and other drill overlays/states: web/src/routes/drill/+page.svelte (sheet markup :1123-1213, sheet CSS :1934-2110, backdrop :1131/:2068, ⋯ popover :1100-1105, done/empty :857-881) and web/src/app.css (html.sheet-open :318-323). Geometry is for 393x852, safe areas 59/34. Sheet top = board-row bottom 504 + 6 = 510px (openSheet :650), which IMG_1388 confirms on the device at CSS 510. 1 CSS px is about 0.166 mm on a 460-ppi 3x iPhone. Text widths were measured with the system SF font through AppKit. Positions were cross-checked against IMG_1388/1389/1391/1392 and the 4:57 PM screenshot (divide displayed px by 2.349, or device px by 3). Those device sheet screenshots predate commit 6033312, which added Expand, the Engine-line pill and the backdrop. Everything else in the sheet still uses the same CSS, and the shared geometry matches to about 1px.

issues.title: Close, Expand, Next and Play are packed into a 92x92px square with 2-6px gaps
issues.evidence: Sheet top = 504 + 6 = 510. Head: 1px border + 6px padding, so buttons span y 517-561. padding-right 6 puts Close at x 343-387; gap 4 puts Expand at 295-339. The step row starts at 561 + 2 (head padding-bottom) + 2 (its own padding) = 565. padding-right 8 puts Play at 393-8-40 = 345-385 (y 567-607); gap 2 puts Next at 299-343 (y 565-609). Gaps: Expand-Close 4px, Next-Play 2px, Expand over Next 4px, Close over Play 6px, Close to Next's corner 4px. That is 0.7mm and 0.3mm on the device. Each target's centre is only 22-25px from a neighbour that does something else. Play is 40x40 (<44). Apple HIG asks for about 12pt around bezeled controls (Play) and about 24pt around borderless ones (chevrons, X). On the device, IMG_1388/IMG_1391 put the X at CSS (365, 539) directly above Play (365, 595) and Next (321, 595); the current build adds Expand directly above Next. The tight layout is now the common one: the uncommitted diff (:1177) dropped the fallback step text, so 'The position' and note-less moves render a 44px row (4-6px gaps; with a 2-line note they are 13-15px).
issues.impact: Next is the most frequent, serial tap. 4px above it are Close (dismisses the sheet and loses the scroll position; getting back = Why? + re-scroll) and Expand (throws the sheet and all its controls up to y 74-166 and hides the board). 2px to its right is Play (starts auto-play instead of one step).
issues.fix: Break the cluster up. (1) Delete the Expand button and add an Apple-style grabber: 36x5 visual, centred in a full-width zone at least 24px tall at the top of the sheet; tap cycles the two heights, drag up expands, drag down collapses or dismisses. (2) Move Prev/Play/Next into a pinned bottom bar (see sheet-exit-6). (3) Leave Close alone at the head's trailing edge with at least 12px clear on every side. Minimal patch if you keep this layout: remove Expand; .sheet-head { padding-bottom: 10px } (Close to Next/Play goes from 4/6px to 12px); .sheet-step { gap: 8px }; .sheet-step .play { width: 44px; height: 44px } (Next 289-333 and Play 341-385, 8px apart).

issues.title: 'Stop drilling this' is permanent, one tap away in a popover that won't close and covers the result box
issues.where: +page.svelte:1100-1105 (details.menu, summary ⋯, .menu-body button), :698-703 skipForGood; CSS .menu summary :1890-1898, .menu-body :1909-1917; src/lib/worker/data.worker.ts:362-363
issues.evidence: The ⋯ is 17.8px glyph + 2x8 padding = 33.8x28 (line-height 28), at x about 353-387, y about 724-752. That is 8px above the right end of Continue (y 760-804; the 4:57 PM screenshot shows the foot row at CSS y 738). The popover: max-width 280 border-box - 24 padding - 2 border leaves 254px, so the 265.6px label wraps to 2 lines, making a 254x40.6 destructive button. The popover spans x 107-387, y about 655-718, drawn on top of the colored result box (z 2 via .foot). A native <details> closes only from its summary, so tapping outside doesn't dismiss it. skipForGood suspends the card and loads the next one immediately, with no confirm. data.worker.ts:363 sets suspended: true, nothing in src ever clears it, and cards.ts:129 filters suspended cards out for good.
issues.impact: A tap that lands 9px high on Continue opens the popover. The natural 'tap the box to dismiss it' then permanently drops the card from the deck, with no undo and no way to restore it.
issues.fix: Make it recoverable: after skipForGood, show an Undo toast for about 6s (44px tall, above the home indicator), and add a 'Stopped cards' list with Restore (Mistakes or Settings). Move the trigger away from Continue, e.g. a full-width 44px row at the end of the Why sheet body ('Stop drilling 3...Bc4'), or the top bar next to the count, and make it 44x44. Replace <details> with a light-dismiss popover (popover attribute, Safari 17+) or a confirm step.

issues.title: The step buttons move up and down between taps as the note length changes
issues.evidence: Row height H = max(44, step-text). step-text = 23.4 (the move-label row, held up by the 23.4px toggle) + 1px gap + 18.9px per note line (14px x 1.35). 0-1 lines give H 44, 2 lines 62.2, 3 lines 81.1. The buttons are centred, so the Next/Prev centre goes 565 + H/2 = 587, 596.1, 605.6: the 44px Next box shifts 9-18.6px from one tap to the next, and the text being read jumps by the same amount. The text column is 247px wide (393-4-44-2-2-44-2-40-8), so a typical 50-character note wraps to 2 lines. The Engine-line pill also slides about 33px sideways as the label grows from '4.Nxd4 · 1/4' (85.9px) to '12...Nxd4 · 10/10' (119.1px).
issues.impact: Repeated Next taps chase a moving target. On note-less moves the buttons rise back to within 4px of Expand/Close.
issues.fix: Pin the controls with .sheet-step { align-items: flex-start }, or better, take them out of the text row (bottom bar, sheet-exit-6). Put the note on its own full-width line (365px instead of 247, so fewer wraps) and reserve its height (min-height: calc(2 * 1.35em)) so the body doesn't jump. Pin the toggle with margin-left: auto.

issues.title: Sheet chips are 36px tall, 6px apart, and shifted sideways from the main chip row they cover
issues.where: +page.svelte:1134-1145 (.sheet-lines chips) vs the main row :907-934; CSS .chip-line :1334-1351, .sheet-lines :1956-1963; scroll-into-view effect :736-741
issues.evidence: Height 36 (:1340) is under 44, and the gap 6 (:1960) is under 8. Width = 42 + SAN, so Nxd4 is 77.8px and Bc4 68.5px (IMG_1388: 12.8-89.4 and 96.2-164). The main row includes Reset and evals: Reset 6-88, 'Nxd4 +0.3' 93-201, 'Bc4 -0.6' 206-306, at y 512-548 (IMG_1389). The sheet opens over it with Nxd4 at 12-90 and Bc4 at 96-164, at y 521-557, the same band. So the sheet's Bc4 lands exactly where the main row's Nxd4 was. The strip is 279px wide (375 - 2x44 - 2x4). With tries (up to 5 chips, about 360px) it overflows with no fade cue, and only the main row auto-scrolls to the selected chip (:736-741).
issues.impact: Tapping where a line was a moment ago selects the other line. Choosing among 36px pills 6px apart takes careful aim.
issues.fix: Keep chips at the same x positions in both places: render the same Reset chip and evals in the sheet, or start the sheet below the main chip row and drop its copy. Give each chip a 44px hit area without changing the look: .chip-line { position: relative } .chip-line::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -4px } with gap 8px. Add an edge fade when the strip overflows, and scroll the selected chip into view.

issues.title: An invisible backdrop turns the whole board into a Close button
issues.evidence: position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index 19; no background; touch-action: none. At the default height it covers 393x510: the top bar, the eval bar and the board (y 123-504), with no dimming. The board still looks live (pieces, coloured arrows), and the hint under it said 'Tap a line to play it, or try any move on the board' (:362). With the sheet open, tapping a piece closes the sheet and the tap is swallowed (no selection). Dragging a piece does nothing at all: a touch that moves fires no click, and touch-action is none. Touches on the same board give two different invisible results.
issues.impact: Trying a move costs an extra tap and dismisses what you were reading. Piece drags silently fail.
issues.fix: Pick one model and make it visible. Preferred: Apple's non-modal sheet. Remove the backdrop at the under-board height so the board stays interactive (tries, piece taps) while html.sheet-open still locks the page; close via X, a grabber swipe, or Continue. Otherwise give the backdrop a visible scrim (background: rgb(0 0 0 / .35)) so 'tap to close' is obvious.

issues.title: No swipe-to-dismiss, no grabber and no Continue in the sheet, so every visit ends with a precise tap
issues.where: CSS .sheet-head/.sheet-step touch-action: none :2080-2083 (no drag handlers anywhere); Close :1155; .sheet.full :2075-2077; the sheet (z 20, :1939) covers the footer (Try again / Why? / Continue, :1108-1116)
issues.evidence: To move on you tap the 44x44 Close at x 343-387, y 517-561 (or the invisible board), then Continue at 760-804. Vertical swipes on the head and step rows do nothing, including on the step note, which reads like part of the explanation. A swipe down at the top of the body is swallowed (overscroll-behavior: contain, :2100). Expanded (top 59 + 8 = 67), Expand/Close sit at y 74-118 and Prev/Next/Play at 122-166, the top 9-19% of the screen, and they step a board that is now hidden. Hoober measured tap accuracy falling from 7mm at the centre to 12mm (about 72px) at the corners. While looking for the main move, the sheet has no 'show it': the only reveal is the 45.8x16.5px inline link in the result box (14px text, padding 0, :1530-1537), which is under the sheet. Apple HIG: 'Include a grabber in a resizable sheet… they can also tap it to cycle through the detents' and 'People expect to swipe vertically to dismiss a sheet instead of tapping a dismiss button.'
issues.impact: Each Why? visit costs a precise mid-screen tap plus a Continue tap. Reading in the expanded state ends with a reach to the top corner.
issues.fix: (a) Grabber plus vertical drag on the head (pointer events: dy > 60px or a fast flick collapses or dismisses; dy < -60px expands). (b) A pinned bottom bar inside the sheet that mirrors the footer, like the equal-width bottom toolbars in the Chess.com and Lichess apps: display: grid; grid-template-columns: 58px 58px 58px 1fr; gap: 8px; padding: 8px 6px calc(12px + var(--safe-b)), with 48px-tall Prev / Play / Next / Continue. 58px is about 9.6mm, Parhi et al.'s minimum for serial one-handed thumb taps. Cells: Prev 6-64, Play 72-130, Next 138-196, Continue 204-387, at y about 758-806, the same band as the footer's Continue, so the thumb finds it in the same place. Repeat Prev/Next while held. While looking for the main move, show 'Show it' next to or instead of Continue. (c) Ignore taps for about 300ms after opening, so a double-tap on Why? (x 116-217) can't fire Play/Next, which open underneath it. Budget: head about 56px (510-566) + bar 102px (750-852) leaves about 184px of body, with the step note moved into the body. That is about the reading area today's 53px step row + 178px body gives.

issues.title: 'Engine line' is an 84x23px pill that also resets your place in the line
issues.evidence: Height = 12px x 1.45 inherited line-height (17.4) + 2x2 padding + 2x1 border = 23.4px. That is under even WCAG 2.5.8's 24px floor; it passes only through the spacing exception, because nothing else is within 12px. Width = 64.2 + 18 + 2 = 84.2. It slides from x 144 to 177 as the move label changes (sheet-drift-3). onclick calls preview(key, 1), so it jumps back to move 1. The label never changes, and the off state is --text-3 grey, which looks disabled.
issues.impact: Hitting it on purpose takes precision, and every tap costs your position in the line.
issues.fix: Keep the look and enlarge the hit area: .engine-toggle { position: relative } .engine-toggle::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -10px -6px } gives 96x43.4. Pin it with margin-left: auto. Show the state in the label ('Line: Book' / 'Line: Engine'), or use a 44px two-option segmented control in the body. Keep the current move when it exists in both lines.

issues.title: Source links are 14px-tall inline text, and usually cut off
issues.evidence: 12px inline anchors are hit-tested on their content area: SF ascent 11.6 + descent 2.53, so about 14.1px tall x about 102-105px wide ('Wikibooks, 3. Nc3' = 102.3), 15.6px apart. The line is nowrap + overflow hidden + ellipsis and starts with the opening name: 'Italian Game: Evans Gambit, McDonnell Defense · as white' takes 328.4px of the 365px line, so every source after it is clipped out of reach (IMG_1392 ends in '· …'). #6b7180 on #15171c is about 3.7:1, below 4.5:1 for 12px text.
issues.impact: The links can't be reached for long opening names, and are fiddly to hit when they do show.
issues.fix: Let the line wrap (white-space: normal). Drop the opening name here or give it its own line. Render each source as a row: .sheet-body .sources a { display: flex; align-items: center; min-height: 44px; font-size: 14px; color: var(--text-2) }.

issues.title: Sheet controls give no pressed feedback, and Next silently does nothing at the end of a line
issues.where: app.css:64 (tap highlight off), app.css:137 (only .btn:active exists); .icon-btn:hover app.css:166-169 and .chip-line:hover :1367-1369 stick on iOS; browse() :446-456
issues.evidence: There are no :active rules for .icon-btn, .chip-line, .play or .engine-toggle, so a tap shows nothing until the board changes, and the iOS sticky-hover grey then stays on the last button tapped. At the last move, step(1) leaves pv.n at its maximum: nothing changes, nothing is disabled, no haptic.
issues.impact: With no confirmation of what was hit, a mis-tap is hard to notice.
issues.fix: .sheet .icon-btn:active, .sheet .play:active, .chip-line:active { background: var(--bg-elev-2); transform: scale(.94) }. Wrap the hover rules in @media (hover: hover). Disable Next at the last move and Prev at the start (.icon-btn:disabled already dims to 0.35). Optionally call feel('move') on each step; click handlers run inside the touch, so the iPhone tick works.

issues.title: Done and empty states use small content-width buttons in the upper half, and 'Preparing your cards…' has no button at all
issues.evidence: Done: margin-top 10vh = 85px puts the card top at about 190. The auto side margins stop the flex stretch, so the card shrinks to about 232px and the buttons to their text: Go again 98.6x44, Done 73.3x44, 10px apart, at y about 315-359. Empty: Get started 116.9x44 at y about 307-351. 'Preparing your cards…' has no button, and the tab bar is hidden on /drill, so the only exit is the 36x36 X in the top-left corner (y 63-99), the hardest spot for a right thumb.
issues.impact: These screens are rare, but they put the next action away from the thumb.
issues.fix: Make the buttons full width and 48px tall (.center { align-self: stretch } or .center .actions { width: 100% }). If you move them down into the thumb zone, add a ~400ms input guard when the screen appears, so a double-tap on the last Continue can't fire Go again (begin() :417-423 resets the session stats). Give 'Preparing your cards…' a 44px 'Back to Today' button.

strengths: The sheet opens exactly under the full-width board (sheetTop = board-row bottom + 6 = 510, openSheet :645-652, confirmed in IMG_1388). The board is never covered or shrunk at the default height, and the sheet's step controls drive that visible board.

Every sheet icon button uses the full global 44x44 .icon-btn. They aren't shrunk like the main move row's 34x34 or the top bar's 36x36, so the sheet's baseline sizes are better than the main screen's.
Opening and closing are double-tap safe. The Why? button's spot (y 760-804) turns into plain body text, and a tap on the backdrop is used up closing the sheet, so no stray move lands on the board.

Closing comes before ending the session. With the sheet open, the backdrop covers the top bar's End-session X, so a stray tap up there only closes the sheet. Escape also closes the sheet before it would end the session (:708-709).

Scrolling is well contained. html.sheet-open (app.css:318-323) locks the page, the sheet body's overscroll-behavior: contain stops scroll chaining, and the chip strip only pans sideways (:2085-2087). The board, page and sheet never fight over a scroll.
The sheet body's bottom padding includes the home-indicator inset (14 + 34 = 48px), so no text or link sits in the home-gesture zone.
The done card appears far from where Continue was, so a double-tap on the last Continue can't hit 'Go again', which would reset the session stats.
Tapping the board to skip the intro is a 381x381px target: the right way to make a frequent action need no aim.
The chips use the same colour coding in the sheet and the main row (green check, red cross, blue dot), so lines are recognisable by colour as well as position.
The 200ms rise animation is short, and it is turned off under prefers-reduced-motion.

home-nav.area: Navigation and home on the phone layout (≤899px): web/src/routes/+layout.svelte (tab bar, top nav, safe areas, main padding, badge), web/src/routes/+page.svelte (Today dashboard), and the lib/ui pieces home renders (InstallHint, AnalysisStatus, LeakCard; ResultBar, LabelChip and Icon are not interactive). VERDICT: the tab bar and the home's Start-drill card are among the best-sized targets in the app. The precision problems here are small: tiny text links, a few areas that look tappable but aren't (or the reverse), no pressed states, iOS zoom on 15px inputs, and the 36px drill exit X (the only navigation once the tab bar hides). None of the debug_photos show home or the tab bar (all 23 images are drill screens), so the geometry below comes from the CSS. Text widths were measured with SF Pro through AppKit (13px 'All' = 15.1px). Safe-area top = 59 is confirmed from the drill X in debug_photos/Screenshot 2026-11-10 at 4.57.09 PM.png. Physical sizes assume 460ppi at DPR 3, so 1 CSS px = 0.166mm and 44px = 7.3mm. Hoober (uxmatters.com/mt/archives/2017/07/design-for-fingers-touch-and-people-part-3.php) measured tap accuracy at about 7mm in the centre of the screen and about 12mm (≈72px) at the corners; list rows should be 9–10mm. Page-y values assume a one-line CTA title; add 64–96px below the CTA when the title wraps to 3–4 lines. THUMB REACH (secondary): the tab bar sits in the natural thumb zone (y 761–818). The CTA is at the top centre, but it's large enough to tap low. Sync is top-right, which suits a rarely used action. The drill exit at top-left is the one bad reach.

issues.where: web/src/routes/drill/+page.svelte:843 (a.icon-btn 'End session'), phone override :2138-2141; the tab bar is hidden in focus mode by web/src/routes/+layout.svelte:34, :73, :206-208. Shared with the drill audit
issues.evidence: `.bar .icon-btn { width: 36px; height: 36px }` shrinks the global 44x44 .icon-btn. 36px = 6.0mm. Position: x 6–42, y 63–99 (main.focus padding-top 59+4 and padding-left 6, +layout.svelte:217-218). Confirmed in Screenshot 2026-11-10 at 4.57.09 PM.png: the X centre at displayed (56,190) x1.28/3 = CSS (24,81) = 6+18, 63+18. Hoober puts tap accuracy at ≈12mm (≈72px) in the corners, so the smallest nav target sits where taps are least accurate, and it's the farthest point from a right thumb. Nothing interactive is within 12px (the board top is ≈124), so a miss does nothing rather than something wrong. Answers are saved when made (drill/+page.svelte:563), so leaving costs little.
issues.impact: Every session ends with a precise reach to the hardest corner. Misses do nothing, so the user has to re-aim or shift their grip.
issues.fix: Restore a 44x44 hit box without moving the glyph or the layout: `.bar .icon-btn { width: 44px; height: 44px; margin: -4px; }`. It still takes a 36x36 layout slot, and the hit box becomes x 2–46, y 59–103. Optionally add 'End session' to the bottom ⋯ menu (drill/+page.svelte:1100) for one-handed exits; inside the menu it can't be hit by accident.

issues.title: Home's 'All' and 'All N' links are 15x19 and 34x19 px of faint text, 9px above a list row
issues.evidence: Measured widths: 'All' at 13px = 15.1px, 'All 57' = 34.0px. Height = 13 x 1.45 = 18.85. That's 2.5x3.1mm, against Apple's 44x44 and WCAG 2.5.5's 44px; they pass WCAG 2.5.8 only through its spacing exception. The link is baseline-aligned in a 32.65px header, so its box ends ≈23.2px down, and the first row (a 343x51.75 link) starts ≈9.5px below it. It's styled like the plain captions: --text-3 #6b7180 on #15171c = 3.7:1 (below 4.5:1 for 13px text), with no underline or chevron. Bigger routes to the same pages already exist: the Lines and Mistakes tabs and the full-width 'Browse all your lines' button (:181).
issues.impact: Users either don't see the links or have to hit a 2.5mm word. A miss opens the first opening in the list instead.
issues.fix:
Remove both 'All' links, since they're redundant. If you want a header shortcut, make the whole header the link: `

Most played as {color}

` with `.list-head { display:flex; align-items:center; min-height:44px; padding:0 10px; border-radius:10px }`. That gives a 343x44 row that behaves like the rows below. For mistakes, replace 'All N' with a full-width `.btn.btn-quiet` 'See all N mistakes' (361x44) under the third card.

issues.title: Focusing the username or token field zooms the whole app on iPhone (15px input text)
issues.where: web/src/app.css:217-226 (.input sets no font-size, so `button, input { font: inherit }` at :91-95 gives the body's 15px from :62). Used in web/src/routes/+page.svelte:68 and routes/settings/+page.svelte:109, :157. Viewport: web/src/app.html:5
issues.evidence: iOS (Safari and Home Screen web apps) zooms in on a text field whose font-size is under 16px and doesn't zoom back out on blur. At 15px the zoom is ≈16/15 = 1.067, so the 393px layout becomes ≈419px wide on screen. The page then pans sideways, and the fixed tab bar is partly off-screen until the user pinches out.
issues.impact: After the first import, or after any Settings edit, every target is offset and the edge tabs (Today, Settings) can be cut off. This persists across screens.
issues.fix: Add `.input { font-size: 16px; }` in app.css (17px would match iOS body text). maximum-scale=1 isn't needed.

issues.title: No touch-down feedback on tabs, list rows, leak cards or text links
issues.where: web/src/app.css:64 (-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent); web/src/routes/+layout.svelte:160-175 (.tabbar a changes colour only); +page.svelte:425-427 (.row:hover only) and :316-318 (CTA :active scale .99); web/src/lib/ui/LeakCard.svelte:81-83 (.leak:hover); app.css:166-169 (.icon-btn:hover)
issues.evidence: The system tap highlight is turned off and these elements only have :hover styles, so nothing changes under the finger. A tab only turns blue after the route changes. On iPhone, :hover sticks after a tap (the sync button keeps its --bg-elev-2 fill). The CTA's scale(0.99) is only 3.6px across 361px. SvelteKit registers a passive touchstart listener on the app root (node_modules/@sveltejs/kit/src/runtime/client/client.js:2126), so :active styles will fire on iOS.
issues.impact: Rows and tabs touch each other, so a near-miss isn't visible until the wrong page opens, and the user can't slide off to cancel.
issues.fix: `.tabbar a:active { color: var(--text) } .tabbar a:active .icon { transform: scale(.88) }`; `.row:active, .leak:has(a.main:active) { background: var(--bg-elev-2) }`; `.drill-cta:active { transform: scale(.98) }`. Wrap the :hover rules in `@media (hover: hover)`. Optional: raise row padding from 10 to 12px (51.75 → 55.75px = 9.2mm) and add 1px dividers.

issues.title: Tab hit areas stop 34px above the screen edge, and inactive labels are low-contrast
issues.where: web/src/routes/+layout.svelte:145-158 (padding-bottom: var(--safe-b) is on the nav, not the links), :160-171 (color var(--text-3))
issues.evidence: Cells are 78.6x57 (13.0x9.4mm), which is fine. But the 34px home-indicator band (y 818–852) belongs to the <nav>, so a low thumb tap there does nothing, and Hoober puts bottom-edge accuracy near 12mm (≈72px). Inactive labels: 11px #6b7180 on #0d0e11 = 3.95:1, below the 4.5:1 WCAG AA needs at that size.
issues.impact: Occasional dead taps on the most-used navigation, and inactive tabs that are hard to read in daylight.
issues.fix: `.tabbar { padding-bottom: 0 } .tabbar a { padding-bottom: var(--safe-b) }`. Each tab becomes 78.6x91 (15mm) and looks the same; taps in that band reach the page, and only an upward swipe from the edge goes home. Use var(--text-2) (#a3a8b3, 8.1:1) for inactive labels. Keep the full-width bar with 5 equal cells; a floating pill inset from the edges would shrink them.

issues.title: Leak cards: about a third is dead space, a blue 'Explained' label looks like a link, and Drill sits 8px from the explorer link
issues.where: web/src/lib/ui/LeakCard.svelte:41-67, CSS :71-108; on home at web/src/routes/+page.svelte:189-191 (also on /leaks)
issues.evidence: The card is ≈361x223. The main link is 335x≈145: the verdict wraps because 'You play Nf6' (88.8) + 8 + the chip (151.3) = 248 > the 225px body, and the 353.9px meta line takes 2 lines. Drill is 59.1x44, 8px below the main link. Not tappable: the 12px padding ring and ≈209x44 of the actions row (335 − 59.1 − 10 − 57.3), about 36% of the card, even though .leak:hover tints the whole card. 'Explained' (12px/600, #7fb2f0) is nearly the link colour (#8ab4f8) and sits 10px from Drill, but does nothing.
issues.impact: Taps on the lower-left of a card or on 'Explained' do nothing, and a slightly high tap on Drill opens the explorer instead.
issues.fix: Use a stretched link so the whole card opens the line: `.leak { position: relative }`, `a.main::after { content:''; position:absolute; inset:0; border-radius:inherit }`, `.actions { position:relative; z-index:1 }`. Give Drill more room: `.drill { min-width: 96px }`, `.leak { gap: 12px }`. Show 'Explained' in --text-3 or as a check icon.

issues.title: Stat cards look like the tappable cards around them but do nothing
issues.evidence: They use the same .card styling (app.css:116-120) as the tappable CTA and list cards. Games is 361x109; As white and As black are 174.5x121. They sit at y ≈323–565, the easiest part of the screen to reach.
issues.impact: Dead taps in the easiest-to-reach area, and mixed signals about what responds.
issues.fix: Link 'As white' and 'As black' to `/lines?c=white|black` (174x121 targets, with an :active state), or drop the border and background so they read as plain numbers.

issues.title: The analysis card's only action is an inline link about 19px tall
issues.evidence: 'Connect Lichess' is 104.5x18.85 (13px x 1.45); 'Reconnect' is 76.3x21.75 (15px). The card stays on home whenever no Lichess token is saved (:17).
issues.impact: A small target, but it stays on the page and is the only way to act on the card.
issues.fix: Put a full-width `.btn.btn-quiet` 'Connect Lichess' (44px tall) under the text, or make the whole card a link to Settings.

issues.title: Install hint has no padding and a 37x20 'Got it' in its corner
issues.where: web/src/lib/ui/InstallHint.svelte:17-26, CSS :30-49 (neither .hint nor .card at app.css:116-120 adds padding)
issues.evidence: 'Got it' is 36.8x20.3 (14px x 1.45) and sits flush against the border and 14px corner radius; the text also touches the border. One tap hides the warning that Safari clears data after 7 days, permanently (localStorage). Its aria-label 'Dismiss' doesn't match the visible 'Got it'. It only appears in a Safari tab, never in the Home Screen app.
issues.impact: First-time Safari visitors get a cramped card with a tiny dismiss target.
issues.fix: `.hint { padding: 14px 16px }`. Make the button `btn btn-quiet` (44px tall), or give it `padding: 12px; margin: -12px` for a ≈61x44 hit box. Drop the mismatched aria-label.

strengths: Tab bar: 5 equal cells of 78.6x57px (13.0x9.4mm) with no gaps or dead zones between them. Each is far larger than its icon and label, and the active tab has a badge and aria-current (+layout.svelte:73-83, :145-175).
Drills are a focus mode with the tab bar hidden (+layout.svelte:34, :206-208), like Chess.com's game and puzzle screens, so no navigation targets compete with the board and footer.
The most frequent action, starting a drill, is the whole 361x134+ CTA card as one link (the play circle is decorative). The bottom Drill tab is a second entry within thumb reach.
Sync is a 44x44 icon button around a 20px glyph, in a corner that's rarely hit by accident. It's disabled and spins while running, so it can't be triggered twice.
Home rows are full-width links (343x51.75), not just the opening name. The Browse button and first-run form use full-width 44–46px controls spaced 10px or more apart.
Home has no horizontal scrollers or chip rows. LeakCard board thumbnails are viewOnly with pointer-events:none (LeakCard.svelte:110-113), so scrolling over them never fights a board.
There are no destructive actions anywhere in nav or home, and drill answers are saved when made (drill/+page.svelte:563), so a stray tab or exit tap costs little.
Safe areas go through --safe-t/--safe-b, and main's bottom padding (58+34+24 = 116px) keeps the last card 24px clear of the tab bar.
SvelteKit preloads links on touchstart, so tab and row taps open almost instantly.

drill-result.area: Drill result state on phones (phase 'result', @media max-width 899px) in web/src/routes/drill/+page.svelte, read as it stands now including the uncommitted edits. Sizes come from the CSS. I checked them by pixel-scanning the iPhone PNGs (1179 px wide, divided by 3 for CSS px). The math matches the device: verdict 660.0-702.3, buttons 760.0-804.0 (762.0-806.0 when the foot is pinned), Play 556-594, move pills 560-590, chips 512-548, drawn board bottom 501.7. 1 CSS px is about 0.166 mm on a 460 ppi, DPR 3 screen.

issues.title: The ⋯ sits 8px above Continue and opens a one-tap, permanent 'stop drilling' button on top of the verdict box
issues.evidence: The summary is 8 pad + ~18 glyph + 8 pad = ~34 wide with line-height 28 (:1894-1898), so it is 34x28 at x 353-387, y 724-752 (ink measured at x 363-376.7, y 737-740). The .foot gap is 8px (:1860), so it sits 1.3mm above Continue (y 760-804), entirely inside Continue's column (x 226.6-387). A tap that lands a little high on Continue's right end opens the menu instead. The popover (absolute, right 0, bottom calc(100% + 6px), max-width 280, :1910-1918) opens at x 107-387, y ~656-720, right over the verdict box (660-702) and 'show it' (~311-362 x 671-691). About 254x41 of its 280x63px (~59%) is the destructive button. A native <details> does not close when you tap outside it, so the popover stays open. The natural 'tap it to dismiss', or a tap meant for 'show it', runs skipForGood: suspendCard sets suspended:true (data.worker.ts:363) and the next card loads immediately. There is no confirm and no undo, and nothing in the app clears suspended. The only way back is Settings > reset ALL drill progress, which itself asks for a second tap (settings/+page.svelte:52-60).
issues.impact: Two plausible taps permanently drop a card from the deck, and the user may never notice.
issues.fix: Move the menu out of the foot: a 44x44 .icon-btn ⋯ at the right end of the top bar (y 63-99, ~700px from Continue), or a row at the bottom of the Why sheet, where 'I play this on purpose' reads naturally after the explanation. Make it two-step like Settings ('Tap again to stop drilling Bc4'), then show a 5s 'Stopped drilling Bc4 · Undo' toast that clears suspended. Use popover=auto (light-dismiss, Safari 17+) or a transparent full-screen backdrop so a tap outside only closes it, and make the item at least 44px tall. Optionally add a Settings list of stopped cards with Restore.

issues.title: The move row crams 34px arrows, 30px move pills 1px apart, and a 38px Play 6px from the next arrow
issues.where: +page.svelte:938-980; CSS :1401-1412 (.navrow gap 2px, .navrow .icon-btn 34x34), :1415-1429 (.play height 38, margin-left 4), :1440-1461 (.moves gap 1px, .mv padding 4px 6px)
issues.evidence: Left to right in 381x38px (y 556-594): prev 34x34 (x 6-40) | 2px | '…' ~26x30 | 1px | '4.Nxd4' 65x30 | 1px | 'Nf6' ~38x30 | 1px | '5.Qe2' ~53x30 | 1px | 'd5' ~30x30 | 2px | next 34x34 (x 266-300) | 6px | Play 80x38 (x 307-387). Pill height is 15 x 1.45 + 2x4 = 29.75px (4.9mm); the gaps are 1-2px (0.17-0.33mm). The arrows are 5.6mm, under Apple's 44pt (7.3mm) and well under the 9.2-9.6mm one-handed thumb targets from Parhi et al. 2006. The 34px override undoes the global 44px .icon-btn (app.css:156-164). The arrows and Play don't even share a height (558-592 vs 556-594). This is the row you use most while reviewing: step, play, jump.
issues.impact: Mis-taps between neighbouring moves, between the strip and the arrows, and between next and Play. The user has to slow down and aim.
issues.fix: Delete the .navrow .icon-btn override so the arrows are 44x44, and set .navrow .play {height:44px; margin-left:8px}; the row grows by 6px to 44. For the moves, either make the strip read-only on phones (pointer-events:none; navigate with the arrows and chips) and show a step label like the Why sheet's '4.Nxd4 · 1/4', or keep pills tappable with .mv {padding:11px 8px} (43.75px tall) and .moves {gap:6px}. Chess.com and Lichess both rely on big back/forward arrows and treat the move strip as secondary. The space comes from result-fit-1.

issues.title: 'show it' is a 45x20px inline text link, and it's the only way to reveal the move after a sound alternative
issues.evidence: A <button> with display:inline is laid out as inline-block, so the hit box is exactly the text. Height is 14 x 1.45 = 20.3px (3.4mm); width is ~7 chars x 6.39px = ~45px, using 6.39px/char measured from a 53-character 14px line in the 4:57 PNG. That is under WCAG 2.5.8's 24px (it only passes through the inline-text exception) and far under 44pt. It sits inside a sentence of plain text, and 'Find it' in the same sentence isn't a control at all. It appears on every 'Good move' result, and when the page overflows the foot can cover it (result-fit-1).
issues.impact: The key choice in this state needs a precise tap on one word.
issues.fix: Make it a real button. Best: in the seeking state the button row becomes [Show it] [Why?] [Continue] at 44-48px, and the box says only 'Masters mostly play another move. Find it on the board.' This depends on result-findit-1 so the board is ready to play. Alternative: keep it in the box as a pill to the right of the one-line message: .seek .text-btn {display:inline-flex; align-items:center; min-height:44px; padding:0 14px; border-radius:999px; background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 16%,var(--bg-elev)); text-decoration:none}. The box grows from 42.3 to ~54px, which fits once the foot-row is gone.

issues.title: The result fits with only 1.7px to spare; misses, reveals and long notes overflow, and the pinned foot then hides text and covers 'show it'
issues.where: +page.svelte:1035-1084 (verdict text), :995-1001 (note); CSS :1296-1300 (.stage gap 16), :1589-1594 (.panel gap 12), :1511-1520 (.note min-height 42), :1856-1865 (.foot sticky with a transparent-to-bg gradient)
issues.evidence: Phone column: 63 (safe top 59 + 4) + 36 bar + 6 + 14 eval bar + 4 + 381 board + 8 + 36 chips + 8 + 38 move row + 8 + 42 note + 16 + 42.3 verdict (1 line) + 12 + 136 foot (10 + 28 streak row + 8 + 44 + 12 + 34) = 850.3 of 852px. The PNGs match: verdict 660.0-702.3, buttons 760.0-804.0. Any extra line overflows. In IMG_1390 a 2-line verdict (660-722.7) already pins the foot (buttons 762-806). Missing the habit with the punish hint: ~142 chars x 6.39px over 351px is 3 lines, plus the hint (18.85 + 4), so the box is 105.8px; with the 100px foot that is 877.8px, 26px of scroll. After Show answer the page always overflows: even a 1-line explanation plus the answer line makes a 66.6px box and, with the 136px foot, 874.6px. With 3 lines it is 915px (63px over), and 'The punishing move here is 4.Nxd4' (~736-756) ends up under the foot, which is pinned at 716 and opaque from 730. The 5:02 PNG shows this on an older build: verdict 147.7px, page scrolled 68px, board top under the status bar. In the seeking state, a 3-4 line note (the 2-line 'Your move is also good…' summary plus a note) pushes 'show it' to ~709-730 while the foot's top is at 716. The foot (z-index 2, with 10px of see-through padding) catches taps on the visible link, leaving only ~6-8px of it tappable.
issues.impact: It breaks the 'fits one screen' rule, hides the answer, puts a dead zone over a link, and adds scrolling right where all the small buttons are.
issues.fix: Free up space and clamp text on phones. Remove the streak row (28 + 8 = 36px): put the streak in the top bar (e.g. 3 small pips or '2/3' next to the count) and move the ⋯ out (result-menu-1). Change .stage gap 16->8, .panel gap 12->8, .foot padding-top 10->8. Clamp .note and .verdict p to 2 lines (display:-webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp:2; overflow:hidden) and keep the full text in Why. Write the eval change as '+2.80 -> +1.75' instead of 'It takes the game from White clearly better (+2.80) to…'. Budget check with 44px chips and move row and 48px buttons: 63+36+6+399+8+44+8+44+8+42+8+42.3+8+(8+48+12+34) = 818.3px, leaving ~34px for one extra line.

issues.title: Double-tapping 'Show answer' lands on Continue and skips the answer
issues.evidence: After a miss the row is [Try again 185.5 | Show answer 185.5], with Show answer at x 201.5-387, y 762-806 (foot pinned) or ~745-789. showMain swaps the row in the same frame for [Try again 100.3 | Why? 100.3 | Continue 160.4] at y 762-806 (pinned). Continue's x 226.6-387 covers 86% of Show answer's width ((387-226.6)/185.5). With width=device-width there is no double-tap-zoom delay, so a bounce or an impatient second tap fires next() before the green arrow has been looked at. The card is requeued, but the learning moment is lost.
issues.impact: The user loses the answer they just asked to see.
issues.fix: Add a ~400ms input guard whenever the button row changes: set armedAt = performance.now() + 400 in showMain and answer, and return early from next/retry/openSheet while performance.now() < armedAt. Or set pointer-events:none on .foot .actions during the 220ms pop animation. Also keep Continue's spot stable: the revealed state can be just [Why?] [Continue], with Try again moved into the Why sheet.

issues.title: Line chips are 36px tall and 5px apart, in a sideways scroller with no edge cue
issues.evidence: Chips are 36px (6.0mm) tall, 82.7-110px wide and 5px (0.8mm) apart (measured 88.7->93.7 and 191.3->196.3 in the 4:57 PNG). The drawn board is 10.3px above and Play 8px below. Reset plus 3 line chips is ~413px, wider than 381, so after a reveal or tried moves the last chip is cut off at x=387 with no fade, leaving a narrow sliver to hit. A wrong chip only previews another line, but this is a frequent target, and Reset must be hit before any move on the board.
issues.impact: Frequent small targets with tight spacing, plus chips you can't see.
issues.fix: Set .chip-line {height:44px}, or keep the 36px pill and extend its hit area (position:relative plus ::after {content:''; position:absolute; inset:-4px 0}). Set .chips {gap:8px}. Add a right-edge fade when the row scrolls (mask-image:linear-gradient(to right,#000 calc(100% - 24px),transparent)). On phones, drop the eval text from the chips if that keeps Reset and 3 chips on screen.

issues.title: The move strip and chip row auto-scroll under the finger
issues.evidence: Every arrow or Play step changes pv, and the effect smooth-scrolls .moves to centre .current. With 30-65px pills, every pill shifts by about one pill per step. Tapping a chip that is cut off at the edge re-centres the chip row the same way. With 1px gaps, a pill has to be re-aimed after every step, and a quick second tap hits whatever slid under the finger.
issues.impact: Targets move just before you tap them.
issues.fix: Scroll only when the target is out of view (offsetLeft < scrollLeft, or offsetLeft + offsetWidth > scrollLeft + clientWidth), and use behavior:'auto' while stepping. Or make the strip read-only on phones (result-nav-1).

issues.title: The chip row appears with the result, so the arrows jump 44px right after you answer
issues.evidence: While you're asked for a move, the move row is at y 512-546 (34px, no Play). When the result appears, the chips take 512-548 and the move row drops to 556-594. A tap aimed at the next arrow (x 266-300) just after answering lands on the second line chip (the habit, ~196-305) and previews that line instead.
issues.impact: The first review tap after answering often hits the wrong control.
issues.fix: Keep a 44px row under the board in every phase (e.g. 'Your move · new · reached 5x' there while asking, the chips afterwards), so nothing below the board moves when the result appears.

issues.title: 'Find it' needs a hidden extra tap on Reset or the previous arrow before the board takes a move
issues.evidence: After a sound alternative, the board shows the position after your move with the opponent to move, and dests is undefined, so dragging a piece does nothing. To 'find it' you first have to hit the 36px Reset chip or the 34px previous arrow, or 'Try again', which throws away the review. The ↻ icon and the 'Reset' label also read like 'retry'.
issues.impact: Following the on-screen instruction fails silently and costs extra small-target taps.
issues.fix: When entering the seeking state, set pv = null (cursor = end) so the drill position is playable at once, with its arrows showing. Try again is then not needed in this state. Rename the chip 'Position' (board or target icon) so it doesn't echo Try again.

issues.title: Try again and Why? are identical grey twins, and 'Try again' is right at its wrap point
issues.evidence: Flex 1:1:1.6 over 381 - 2x10 = 361px gives 100.3 | 100.3 | 160.4. The content box is 100.3 - 2x18 = 64.3px, and the 'Try again' ink at 15px/600 measures 64.3px. That measurement is from the 4:57 PNG, where that build's row measured 106.3 | 106.3 | 148.3. So the label wraps to 'Try / again' or touches the padding. The two quiet buttons share colour and size. Try again (retry() at :631-642 clears the result, tried moves and selected line) sits 10px from the harmless Why?. Otherwise the sizes and the 10px gaps meet HIG and WCAG.
issues.impact: Hitting Try again instead of Why? wipes the review, and the label may render on two lines.
issues.fix: Use at most two buttons per state: seeking [Show it] [Continue] (Why? as a 44px row under the verdict or in the top bar); revealed and correct [Why?] [Continue]; Try again only after a miss. If three stay, set .btn {white-space:nowrap; padding:0 12px} and give Try again an icon or outline style so it isn't a twin of Why?. Consider 48px height, since Hoober's studies found taps near the screen edges are less accurate than mid-screen.

issues.title: Hover styles stick after a tap, and chips, arrows, move pills, Play and ⋯ have no pressed state
issues.evidence: iOS keeps :hover on the last element you tapped. button.mv:hover uses the same style as .mv.current, so after tapping a move and stepping on, two moves look current. The last-tapped arrow keeps a grey square (visible in IMG_1383). -webkit-tap-highlight-color:transparent removes the system highlight, only .btn has :active (app.css:137-139), and haptics fire only for board moves and results (:554, :578). Small targets give no instant confirmation, so mis-taps go unnoticed.
issues.impact: Users can't tell what their tap hit.
issues.fix: Wrap hover rules in @media (hover:hover). Add :active (scale(0.96) or a tinted background) to .chip-line, .navrow .icon-btn, .mv, .play and summary. Optionally call feel('move') on arrow and Play taps.

issues.title: The '…' (whole game) button sits 2px from the previous arrow and can't be undone
issues.evidence: It is ~26x30px at x 42-67, 2px to the right of the previous arrow (6-40). It sets fullPath = true, which only resets on the next card (:391), and it changes the whole strip.
issues.impact: A slightly-off tap on the previous arrow rewrites the move strip for the rest of the card.
issues.fix: Hide it on phones (step back with the previous arrow instead), or give it a 44px box at least 8px from the arrow.

issues.title: Thumb reach (secondary): safe and risky targets are in the wrong zones
issues.evidence: Continue at the bottom right (226.6-387 x 760-804) is in the easy right-thumb zone, which is good. But the ⋯, the gateway to a destructive action, is in that same zone. The previous arrow at the far left of mid-screen (6-40 x 558-592) is the hardest frequent target for a right thumb. The top-left X is a rare exit (results are saved on answer), so it is rightly far away.
issues.impact: The easiest spot to hit holds a dangerous control, and a frequent control is the hardest to reach.
issues.fix: Move the ⋯ to the top bar. If navigation moves into a bottom toolbar (Chess.com/Lichess style), make previous and next wide segments (at least 80x48) in the lower third, and keep Continue at the bottom right.

strengths: The bottom buttons are real 44px .btn targets with 10px gaps, stretched to 100-228px wide. They are the biggest targets on the screen and have a press scale (:active, app.css:137-139).

The sticky foot keeps the buttons in the same place in every state (measured 760.0-804.0 in the 4:57 PNG, and 762.0-806.0 in IMG_1390 and the 5:02 miss PNG), so Continue is always bottom-right under the thumb.

issues.title: A slip on the board instantly commits a graded answer, with no undo
issues.evidence: Squares are 381/8 = 47.6px (≈7.9mm) with 0px between them. Hoober's data puts the minimum at 11mm ≈ 66px at the top of the screen, which is where the far ranks are (y 123-171). Legal destinations often touch: a pawn's single and double push (e3/e4) share an edge, and a bishop's neighbouring diagonal squares share a corner. Board.svelte:86 keeps chessground 9.2.1's drag defaults (dist/state.js:45-46: distance 3, autoDistance true). drag.js:45 sets `started: autoDistance && stats.dragged`, and drag.js:165 turns stats.dragged on after any drag move. From then on every touch on a piece is a live drag from the first pixel, and releasing 1px over a neighbouring legal square is a move (drag.js:159). Tap-tap commits on the touchstart of the second tap (board.js selectSquare -> userMove), so you can't slide off to cancel. The first answer is saved immediately (+page.svelte:564-565 data().record(card.card.id, firstTry)), and recordAnswer (src/lib/drill/cards.ts:105) sets streak 0 on a miss ('Back to 0'). Nothing can undo it.
issues.fix: (1) Board.svelte config: `draggable: { enabled: !!dests, distance: 10, autoDistance: false }`. A tap that rolls under 10px (≈1.7mm, about Android's 8dp touch slop) stays a tap, and the threshold never drops to 0. Lichess's phone app keeps a fixed 3px but adds a target circle; turning autoDistance off is the key part. (2) Add 'Undo' for a slip after a wrong first answer. The page still holds the pre-answer record in `card.card`, so a worker `restore(record)` (db.cards.put) plus `recorded = false; stats.done--; firstTry = true; retry()` is enough. To keep it from becoming a free retry, show it only when the wrong move starts on the same square as an accepted answer and lands on a square touching that answer's square (e2e3 vs e2e4, Bf1d3 vs Bf1c4). (3) Optional setting in Settings > Drills: 'Move with: Tap squares / Drag / Both' (Chess.com's 'Move Method' and Lichess's pieceShiftMethod offer this). Tap squares means `draggable.enabled: false`, which removes accidental drag moves entirely.
issues.impact: A thumb slip, such as a pawn to e3 instead of e4 or a piece dropped one square off, is graded as a miss and wipes the card's streak. It can happen on every card, which makes it the most expensive mis-tap in the drill.

issues.title: 'Tap the board to skip' does nothing on most of the board
issues.evidence: The skip is a `click` handler on the board wrapper. Chessground's touchstart handler calls e.preventDefault() whenever the touch is on a piece or within one square of any piece centre (drag.js:23-25; radiusSq = (W/8)^2 = 47.6px, drag.js:71). The Touch Events spec says that when touchstart is cancelled, 'no mouse or click events will be fired', so the click never arrives. During the replay the board also can't select or drag (dests is undefined outside ask/result, +page.svelte:367-369 -> Board.svelte:80,86-87), so the tap does nothing at all. Only empty spots more than 47.6px from every piece respond: about 40% of the board in the start position (ranks 4-5 plus parts of 3 and 6), about 25% in the IMG_1388 position. Touching a piece, the natural move when you already know the answer, never skips. The replay lasts up to 5.8s (+page.svelte:60-62, 425-435) on every card. Desktop isn't affected because preventDefault on mousedown doesn't cancel the click.
issues.fix: Use pointer events, which a cancelled touchstart can't suppress: on the wrapper, `onpointerdown={() => { if (phase === 'intro' || (phase === 'ask' && cursor < end)) { goTo(end); flushSync(); } }}` (flushSync from 'svelte'). Current Safari fires pointerdown before touchstart, so flushing the Board config first means touching your own piece both skips the replay and picks the piece up in one touch. Verify that on the device. The same handler fixes drill-ask-6. Quick check on the phone today: during a replay, tap a pawn (nothing happens), then tap an empty square on rank 4 or 5 (it skips).
issues.impact: Skipping the replay, done on nearly every card, works only if you hit an empty patch in the middle of the board. Otherwise the tap is silently ignored, which is exactly 'you need to be precise'.

issues.title: Move chips are 30px tall and 1px apart, in a scroller 10px under the board
issues.evidence: Height = 15px x 1.45 (app.css:62) = 21.75 + 2x4 padding = 29.75px. Width = text + 12px ≈ 29-65px ('4.Nxd4' 65x29, '2...Bf5' 62x29, the review's '...' ≈ 24px). Gaps are 1px between chips and 2px to the chevrons. While answering, about 7 chips plus ‹ › share a 381x34 strip: roughly 9 targets about 42px wide, 1-2px apart. Chip tops are at y≈514, 10px below the own back rank (y 457-504), where development and castling moves land. Tapping a chip jumps the board back (goTo, :943) and quietly turns off answering. Aiming at a chip and landing high on the back rank while a piece is selected makes a move.
issues.fix: Make chips at least 44px tall with 6-8px gaps or more, e.g. `.mv { min-height: 44px; padding: 0 10px } .moves { gap: 6px }`. Grow hit areas only downward or sideways, never up into the board. The review screen already fills 852px (Continue ends at y≈806, plus 12+34 footer padding), so take the extra 6px from elsewhere, e.g. .note min-height 42 -> 36. While answering, consider showing the game moves as plain text and keeping only ‹ › and '?' as targets.
issues.impact: This is the tightest cluster of buttons in the drill, used constantly in the review and sometimes while answering. Hitting the neighbour 1px away loses your place.

issues.title: While dragging, the piece and the target square are hidden under the thumb
issues.evidence: drag.js:124-127 moves the dragged piece to (touch - W/16), so a 47.6px piece sits centred under a 16-20mm fingertip, covering a 7.9mm square. Chessground 9 adds no class to the square under the finger (render.js only marks selected, move-dest and last-move), and the ≈13px destination dots are also under the thumb. Lichess's phone app (flutter-chessground board_settings.dart) defaults to dragFeedbackScale 2.0 and dragFeedbackOffset (0,-1), which draws the carried piece twice as big and one square up. Its DragTargetKind.circle is 'A circle twice the size of a board square', centred on the square under the finger, which is still where the piece drops.
issues.fix: In Board.svelte, add a passive document touchmove listener. While cg.state.draggable.current?.started, take the square from cg.getKeyAtDomPos([x,y]) and place an absolutely positioned ring two squares wide (95px) on it, green if it's a legal destination. Lift and enlarge the carried piece with CSS: `.board :global(cg-board piece.dragging) { width: 20%; height: 20%; margin: -15% 0 0 -3.75% }` draws it 1.6 squares wide, centred on the finger and just above it. This works because chessground's inline transform is a pure translate; a CSS `scale` would break it. The ring shows the real drop square, so the lifted piece doesn't mislead.
issues.impact: Drag users drop blind. The square under the thumb gets the move, and with drill-ask-1 that becomes a graded miss.

issues.title: ‹ › are 34px with a 4.5x9px glyph, and › moves 86px left in the review, 6px from Play
issues.evidence: `.navrow .icon-btn { width: 34px; height: 34px }` shrinks the global 44x44. Icon 18 draws a 4.5x9px chevron with no background, and people aim at what they see. 2px gaps to the chips. While answering, › sits at x 353-387. In the review, Play (≈80x38) takes x≈307-387 and › moves to x≈267-301 (IMG_1389), 6px from Play (margin-left 4 + gap 2). Tapping where › used to be starts autoplay. `.icon-btn:hover` (app.css:166-169) keeps its background after a tap on iOS (sticky › in IMG_1383), and there's no :active state. The Why sheet's chevrons are already 44px (+page.svelte:1161, 1180).
