Keep them in the same place in every phase: pin › to the right edge and move Play left of the moves or into the footer. Keep at least 8px between targets. Wrap hover rules in @media (hover: hover) and add :active backgrounds. Add touch-action: manipulation on .navrow so quick repeated taps can't be read as a double-tap zoom.
issues.impact: Stepping is the main review control and the only way to browse while answering. Tiny, shifting targets cause misses and Play-instead-of-› taps.

issues.title: '?' looks tappable but isn't; after stepping back the board silently refuses moves, and the way back is a 20px text link
issues.evidence: '?' is a <span> styled as an accent chip (≈20-32 x 29.75px) with no handler. After ‹ or a chip, cursor < end, so dests is undefined (:367-369) and trying to move does nothing, with no message. The only labelled way back is .text-btn 'Back to the position': no padding, 14px x 1.4 = 19.6px tall x ≈136px wide, on the note's third line at y≈596-615.
issues.fix: Make '?' a 44x44 button that calls goTo(end). While answering, a touch on the board when cursor < end returns to the position: the same onpointerdown + flushSync handler as drill-ask-2, so that touch lands on a board you can move on. If the link stays, make it a 44px-tall button.
issues.impact: A stray chip tap leads to a dead end: you try to move, nothing happens, and you have to find a small link.

issues.title: The move row re-centres after every tap and every replay step, so chips slide under the finger
issues.evidence: The effect depends on [pv, cursor, phase, selected, lines] and always calls row.scrollTo({ left: chip.offsetLeft - (row.clientWidth - chip.offsetWidth)/2, behavior: 'smooth' }). During the replay the cursor advances every 600ms, so the row is often mid-scroll. In the review, every chip tap slides that chip to the centre, moving the neighbours you're about to tap by up to half the row (≈110-150px). There's no edge padding or fade, so half-clipped chips sit 2px from ‹ and › ('5.Be...' in the 5.02 screenshot, 'dxe...' in IMG_1382).
issues.fix: Scroll only when the current chip is outside the visible area, with about one chip of margin, and use behavior 'instant' during the replay. Add 12-16px inline padding and a mask-image fade at both ends of .moves, plus scroll-snap-type: x proximity.
issues.impact: Tapping two moves in a row, or a move during the replay, often hits whatever slid under the finger.

issues.title: Close X is 36x36 with a ~10px glyph (fine where it is; keep it isolated)
issues.evidence: 36 is below the 44px HIG, and the X ends the session without confirmation. But it's alone in the top-left corner (x 6-42, y 63-99), 24px above the board with the non-interactive eval bar in between, and nothing tappable sits beside it. It's a deliberate reach for a right thumb, which suits a session-ending action.
issues.fix: Optional: grow the hit area to 44x44 by extending up and left only, so the 24px buffer above the a8/h8 squares stays. Don't put anything next to it.
issues.impact: Missing it is cheap and hitting it by accident is unlikely, so this is low priority.

issues.title: No haptic for engine-checked answers, and no pressed state on the small buttons
issues.evidence: For moves not in the saved data, answer() waits for evaluate(next.frame.fen, 14) (:546) before calling feel() (:554). That's seconds after the touch, and Board.svelte:45-47 notes that iPhone only plays haptics during a touch, so these answers get no tick while a faint 'Checking...' shows. -webkit-tap-highlight-color is transparent everywhere and .icon-btn/.mv have no :active style, so a tap on ‹ › or a chip shows nothing until the board changes.
issues.fix: Call feel('move') synchronously in onMove, inside the touch, for every answer; keep the verdict tick for known moves. Add :active backgrounds to .icon-btn, .mv and .play.
issues.impact: Without confirmation, people re-tap or doubt the tap landed, which means more taps that need precision.

issues.title: Capture targets are nearly invisible
issues.evidence: An empty destination gets a ≈13px dot (19% of the 33.7px corner distance ≈ 6.4px radius, alpha 0.5). An occupied destination gets only a ring at alpha 0.3 (square.oc.move-dest), barely visible on #8ca2ad/#dee3e6: e5 after selecting Nf3 in the IMG_1384 video frame at 0:00.
issues.fix: Use a stronger, thicker capture ring (alpha 0.55-0.6) or corner wedges like Lichess.
issues.impact: If you can't see that a capture is legal, you aim less confidently.

issues.title: The board stops 6px short of each screen edge
issues.evidence: Board = 393 - 2x6 = 381 -> 47.6px squares. Edge to edge it would be 393/8 = 49.1px (+3.1%, ≈8.1mm), as in Chess.com's phone app.
issues.fix: On phones in the drill, set main.focus side padding to 0 and give the top bar, move row, note and footer their own 6px inline padding. The board grows 12px taller, so take 12px back in the review elsewhere (e.g. .drill gap 6->4, .note min-height 42->36, foot padding-top 10->6).
issues.impact: A free 3% on every square, the most-tapped target in the app, without shrinking anything.

issues.title: While answering, every control is in the top 72% of the screen and the bottom 256px is empty
issues.where: /Users/jwahbeh/chess-trainer/web/src/routes/drill/+page.svelte:841-1009; the panel is empty on phones while answering (.title/.desktop hidden, :2130-2146)
issues.evidence: Targets while answering: X y 63-99, board 123-504, move row 512-546, link up to ≈615. The page ends ≈612 and y≈612-852, the easiest thumb zone, is empty. The far rank (y 123-171) is the hardest one-handed reach. In the review the footer buttons sit at y≈762-806.
issues.fix: Keep the board exactly where it is; it doesn't move between ask and the review, which is good. Use the empty bottom for answer-phase controls, as Chess.com's and Lichess's bottom toolbars do: a bar at the footer's height (y≈762-806) with a wide 'Skip' during the replay and big ‹ › (about 25% of the width x 44-48px) while answering. Put Skip, not a chevron, under Continue's footprint, so a double-tap on Continue only skips the next replay. For far squares, tap-tap is easier than a long stretched drag.
issues.impact: Secondary, as you asked. Moving the small controls to the bottom also fixes their size.

strengths: The board is full width (381px, so 47.6px squares, above the 44px HIG) and stays at y 123-504 through intro, ask, checking and the review. The top bar keeps its 36px height, and answering adds rows below the board, never above, so a follow-up tap lands on the same squares.

Input is forgiving where it can be. Tapping a non-legal square just deselects (chessground userMove -> unselect). A drag is cancelled by dropping it back on its square or off the board (deleteOnDropOff is false). A second finger cancels a drag.
Castling works as king->g1 or king->h1 (chessgroundDests lists both, normalizeMove at +page.svelte:523), so the target is effectively bigger.
Auto-queen (+page.svelte:522) means no small promotion picker in the middle of a drill.
touch-action: none on the board (Board.svelte:121) means drags never fight page scroll or zoom, and the answer screen (≈612px) never scrolls.
The session-ending X is alone in the top-left corner, 24px from the board with the non-interactive eval bar as a buffer, far from anything you tap often.
The haptic tick fires inside the touch (Board.svelte:45-67, settle on touchstart/touchend), confirming the move registered without a double report.
Continue's footprint (y≈762-806) is empty during the next card's replay and answer, so a double-tap on Continue can't trigger anything.
The answer screen is uncluttered: no arrows or eval until you answer, a dimmed empty eval bar, last-move highlight, and legal-move dots when a piece is selected.
The Why sheet's step chevrons are already full 44x44 .icon-btn (+page.svelte:1161, 1180), a ready model for the move row.

Method: CSS math, with SF Pro string widths measured from the macOS system font through JXA NSString sizeWithAttributes (accurate to about 2px). debug_photos has no shots of these screens: all 25 images are drills. IMG_1388 was used to check the global .segmented on the real device, because the drill used that same class at commit de9fafb (16:13) and the photo is from 16:21. A live render wasn't possible: headless Chrome was refused by the sandbox. Settings y-values (document coordinates; the page scrolls) assume Lichess is connected; when it isn't, add about 70-170px below the Lichess group. Repo not modified.

issues.title: Every segmented control is a row of 32px slivers with a dead rim and a selection you can barely see
issues.where: app.css:175-199 (.segmented, .segmented button, [aria-pressed]); used at leaks:63, lines:41, settings:129/172/188/194/206, bench:109/117
issues.evidence: Buttons are 32px tall with 0 14px padding and 14px text, inside a track with 3px padding and 2px gaps. So each control looks like a 38px pill but only the inner 32px responds; a tap on the 3px rim or a 2px seam hits the track (nothing happens, or iOS snaps it to a neighbour, which is just as wrong). Narrowest segments: All 17.3+28 = 45.3px, 2× 45.7, 3× 46.0, On 47.2. Period is 288.2x38 visible but 274.2x32 live, so 20% of it is dead. Checked on the device: the drill used this same class at commit de9fafb (16:13) and IMG_1388 is from 16:21. Its track is 114 device px = 38 CSS px and its segment 96 px = 32 CSS px. The selected segment is #15171c, the same as the background, on a #1c1f26 track: 1.09:1 contrast. The only cue left is label brightness (#e9eaee vs #a3a8b3, 1.98:1). There are 7 of these on the secondary screens (5 on Settings), and none has a pressed state.
issues.fix: In app.css under @media (max-width: 899px): .segmented { display:flex; width:100%; padding:0; gap:0 } .segmented button { flex:1; height:44px; padding:0 6px; border:3px solid transparent; background-clip:padding-box; border-radius:11px }. That gives a 38px visible pill, a 44px hit area and no dead seams. Selected: background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 18%, var(--bg-elev-2)); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px var(--accent) (7.8:1 against the track). Add :active { background-color: var(--bg-elev) }. Settings needs .segmented { align-self: stretch } on phones; Lines' header needs flex-wrap or a flex:1 control. Resulting widths: Period 72.2px per segment, Reach 90.3, Speed 120.3, Order and Haptics 180.5, Mistakes colour 120.3. Haptics On/Off works better as a full-row switch, the way Chess.com and iOS Settings do it.
issues.impact: The densest small targets on these screens. Mis-taps on Period, Reach or time controls start heavy background work (secondary-6); a mis-tap on a colour filter collapses expanded families (lines:31) or resets Show more (leaks:48-52).

issues.title: Explore's move crumbs and continuation moves are 34px chips 2px apart, in a scroller that loses the current move
issues.evidence: padding 6px 9px on 15px text gives 6+21.75+6 = 33.75px tall. Widths are label + 18: e5 36.1, a6 36.2, 1.e4 47.6, 2.Nf3 58.1, 3.Bb5 60.5. Gap is 2px, and wrapped continuation rows are also 2px apart. Start plus the first 6 moves take 351.5px of 361, so from the 7th move on the current crumb is off the right edge. Nothing scrolls it into view, and mask-image fades the last 8% (29px) even when scrolled to the end. A mis-tap jumps to another position and adds a history entry.
issues.fix: .crumb, .ply { min-height:44px; padding:11px 10px } .crumbs, .mainline { gap:6px } (8px for the wrapping continuation moves). After each navigation set crumbs.scrollLeft = crumbs.scrollWidth (or scroll .current into view with block:'nearest'), and only fade the side that has hidden moves. Better still, one 44px strip like Chess.com's move list: played moves, the current one highlighted, your usual continuation dimmed after it, so 'forward along my line' is a single tap.
issues.impact: The main way to move around on Explore; small targets inside a sideways scroller.

issues.title: Explore's step buttons are four 44px icons 6px apart, and Start (which wipes the line) sits next to Back
issues.evidence: 4x44 + 3x6 = 194px, centred: Start 99.5-143.5, Back 149.5-193.5, Forward 199.5-243.5, Flip 249.5-293.5, at y 480-524. The buttons have no background (only :hover paints one), so you aim at 20px icons 50px apart without seeing the edges. Start runs go([]), which truncates the path: the crumbs collapse to 'Start' and the line survives only in browser history, and the manifest is display: standalone, so there's no Safari Back. Back also drops the move you undo, and Forward is 'most common move', not redo, so Back then Forward can land somewhere else.
issues.fix: On phones: .controls { display:grid; grid-template-columns:44px 1fr 1fr 44px; gap:12px }, with visible button backgrounds. Back and Forward each become (361-88-36)/2 = 118.5x48, with Start and Flip 12px away at the ends; or make Start a long-press on Back, as in the Chess.com and Lichess apps. Keep the whole line and move a cursor through it: Back and Start delete nothing, Forward replays your line, future crumbs show dimmed. Option: on Explore, hide the tab bar and put these controls in a bottom toolbar (thumb zone), like Chess.com's analysis bar.
issues.impact: The most-used controls on Explore; one slip loses a 10+ move line with no way back.

issues.title: Explore on a phone: no move row on screen, scrolling pushes the board away, and the board can't be scrolled
issues.where: explore/+page.svelte:107-222 (single column below 900px); lib/ui/Board.svelte:121 (touch-action: none); chessground dist/drag.js start()
issues.evidence: Document y: title 75-99, board 109-470, controls 480-524, crumbs 540-576, reach block 590-683 (30px count 43.5 + wrapped line 21.75 + gaps + 8px bar), 'YOUR MOVES' 703-722, first move row 736-779, and the tab bar starts at 760. So no complete row is visible. Once you scroll down to the list, the board (where the tapped move plays; go() uses noScroll) is off screen. touch-action: none turns the whole 361x361 board, 42% of the 852px screen, into a zone where a swipe can't scroll. Chessground on its own would only block scrolling when the touch starts on or next to a piece.
issues.fix: Keep the board full width but pin it: @media (max-width:899px) { .board-col { position:sticky; top:0; padding-top:var(--safe-t); z-index:2; background:var(--bg) } }. The pinned block is 59+24+10+361+10+44 = 508px, which leaves about 250px (crumbs + 4 rows) of moves scrolling underneath; that's how the Chess.com and Lichess explorers work. Put 'Your moves' directly under the controls (.reach { order:1 }), or fold the reach block into one line such as '1,234 games · 52%'. If the board isn't pinned, give Explore's Board a prop that sets touch-action:auto and let chessground decide when to block scrolling.
issues.impact: Every list on Mistakes and Lines leads here, and right now each move needs a scroll.

issues.title: Reset drill progress and Clear stored games are small text buttons whose second tap lands in the same spot; Disconnect has no confirmation
issues.evidence: .danger has 6px 0 padding on 15px text: 33.75px tall, 138.8px (Reset) and 139.2px (Clear) wide, drawn as red text. The first tap arms it, and the label grows rightwards to 245.3 / 256.7px from the same left edge. confirmReset and confirmClear never time out. So a double tap, or two taps at the same point, confirms. Reset wipes every card's streak (data().resetCards()); Clear deletes every stored game, which then has to be downloaded again. Disconnect (116.8x44) drops the Lichess token immediately, and reconnecting takes the full OAuth round trip.
issues.fix: Move them into a final 'Danger zone' group as full-width 44px rows. Confirm in a bottom sheet or dialog with Cancel in the thumb zone and the red confirm somewhere other than where the first tap landed (e.g. 'Reset 232 cards'). If you keep tap-twice, disarm after about 4s and ignore a second tap within about 600ms. Give Disconnect the same confirmation.
issues.impact: Rarely used, but the loss is permanent.

issues.title: Filter taps on Settings immediately start expensive background work
issues.evidence: A time-control chip (59.8x34 or wider, 8px gap) calls applyFilter(), which runs setFilter and then analyze(), restarting the Stockfish analysis. A Period segment (45.3-61.7 x 32, 2px gap) that widens the period, e.g. All (2px from 2 yr), calls sync() to download more months from Chess.com, and tapping back doesn't cancel it. A Reach segment (45.7-53 x 32, 2px gap) calls analyze(), and a lower threshold means more positions to evaluate on the phone.
issues.fix: 44px targets (secondary-1, plus .chip { height:44px; padding:0 16px }, which still fits on one 300.4px row). Apply filter changes about 1.5s after the last tap, with an 'Applying...' note. Ask 'Download all N months?' before widening to All. Let a later tap cancel a sync or analysis that's already running.
issues.impact: One slip costs battery, data and minutes of background work.

issues.title: The only way out of Explore is a tab, and the tab resets Lines and Mistakes
issues.where: explore/+page.svelte (no back button); lib/format.ts:8-9 exploreHref; routes/+layout.svelte:14-20 (tab links); lines:16 open; leaks:22-24 list/habitsShown
issues.evidence: The tabs link to plain /lines and /leaks. Coming back that way resets the colour to White/All, collapses expanded families (open), drops extra Show more pages (habitsShown/oneOffsShown) and scrolls to the top. The manifest is display: standalone, so there's no Safari Back. Even a history back can't restore a deep scroll on Mistakes: list starts as null and loads asynchronously, so the page is still short when the scroll position is restored. Variation rows (0px apart) and card links are easy to hit by accident, and each slip costs your place.
issues.fix: Add a 44x44 back chevron at the left of Explore's title row: history.back() when the previous page was in the app (afterNavigate's from), otherwise a link to where the user came from. Export a SvelteKit snapshot from the Lines and Mistakes pages that saves open, habitsShown/oneOffsShown and scrollY, and restore the scroll once list has loaded. Make the tab links remember the last ?c.
issues.impact: Makes every mis-tap on a list screen more expensive.

issues.title: Lists move under your finger while analysis is running
issues.where: leaks/+page.svelte:18, :28-45 (list replaced at most every 15s while analysis runs; sorted by points, lib/worker/data.worker.ts:280); explore/+page.svelte:34-45 (refetches on analysis.version, which bumps at most every 2.5s, state.svelte.ts:209-212)

issues.title: Settings fields use 15px text, so iOS zooms the page when you tap them

strengths: Lines rows are model targets: family rows 359x64.2 with 10px between buttons, variation rows 343x53.75, and 'Explore the tree' 343x43.75. The whole row is tappable, with aria-expanded and a rotating chevron. Copy this pattern to Settings.
The global sizes are right where they're used: .btn is 44px tall, .icon-btn 44x44, .input 46px. Show more is a full-width 361x44 button and the Developer row is 361x70.6.

LeakCard thumbnails don't get in the way of scrolling: .thumb { pointer-events: none } (LeakCard.svelte:110-113) carries through to the chessground board, so Board.svelte's touch-action: none never applies and a swipe on a thumbnail scrolls the list. The whole upper card (335 x 115+) is one link.
Explore's board fills the content width (361px, 45.1px squares, above 44), and move rows are full-width buttons (361x43.2): you tap the whole row, not just the move.

The dangerous settings already have a two-step confirmation and sensible disabled states: Switch stays disabled until the name changes, the last time control can't be turned off, Reset and Clear are disabled when there's nothing to clear.
Tab bar targets are 78.6x57, with the 34px home-indicator strip kept as padding, and page content stops 24px above the bar.
The time-control chips show their selected state clearly (accent fill, app.css:211-215). That's the look to reuse for the selected segment.
Mistakes shows 24 cards at a time, so a long list stays light on a phone.

results.measured: Navrow in the result phase (y 556-594). Moves (.mv): padding 4+4 (drill:1453) + 15px x 1.45 line-height inherited via button font:inherit (app.css:62, 91-95) = 29.75 tall (4.9 mm at 6.04 px/mm). Width = SAN + 12, so 'd5' is 18+12 = 30. Gap 1px (drill:1444), so the pitch is 31px (5.1 mm). Arrows 34x34 (drill:1407-1411 overrides app.css:159-160), 2px from the scroller (drill:1403). Play 38 tall (drill:1419), 2+4 = 6px from the next arrow (drill:1403, 1420). Move scroller = 381-34-2-2-34-2-4-79 = 224px (x 42-266). Chips 36 tall (drill:1340), 5px gaps (drill:1324). IMG_1389 (x0.4258 CSS px per displayed px): '4.Nxd4' box at y 560-589 (29px); Play 556-593 tall x 307-386 wide (79px); chips 512-547 tall, 82 / 110.7 / 101 wide, gaps 5.7 / 6px. My own inventory of sub-44px selectors visible on a phone in standalone mode: about 26 (drill 14, home 2, lines 2-3, leaks 2, explore 2-3, settings 5; bench reuses .segmented). 10 of them are under 24px: the home 'All' links, Connect Lichess, Reconnect, Change, the token text-btn, the token link, Back to the position, show it, the engine toggle, and the source links. The audit's '24 / 9' slightly undercounts but reaches the same conclusion.
results.note: Inventory corrections. (1) InstallHint 'Got it' never renders in the Home Screen app (InstallHint.svelte:8 requires ios && !standalone). (2) .note-link and .line-source .text-btn are desktop-only (storyBlock is behind {#if !narrow}, drill:1086). (3) Tab links are 78.6x57, not 58: 92px border-box minus 34 safe-area pad minus 1px border-top (+layout:151-156). Root cause worth naming: the global reset button { padding: 0 } (app.css:97-102) makes every unclassed button exactly its 20.3px text line. Two nits on the fix. .moves is display:flex with the default align-items (stretch), so .moves { align-self: stretch } alone already stretches the .mv buttons. And the row is 38px only when Play renders (result phase with a selected line, drill:966); while asking it is 34px.

results.measured: Confirmed. -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent is set on html/body and inherits (app.css:64). :active exists only on .btn (app.css:137-139) and .drill-cta (+page:316-318). There are 14 :hover selectors; 12 can be reached on a phone. The other two: .top nav a:hover (+layout:130) is in the header hidden under 900px, and .note-link:hover (drill:1778) is desktop-only. IMG_1383 (Nov 9 build) shows a roughly 33x33 grey square stuck behind the next arrow at CSS x 306-339, y 211-244, which is app.css:166. REFUTED: the claim that a touch listener exists only by accident, so .btn:active never fires on Settings, Lines or Home. SvelteKit 2.70.4's router runs container.addEventListener('touchstart', tap, { passive: true }) with container = document.documentElement (node_modules/@sveltejs/kit/src/runtime/client/client.js:361 and 2126). setup_preload() is called at 2700-2703 unless navigator.connection.saveData is set, and Safari has no navigator.connection. So every page already has a root touchstart listener: .btn:active works everywhere, and the proposed ontouchstart / empty-listener fix does nothing.
results.note: The real gap is CSS only. Add :active styles with a 0ms transition to .icon-btn, .chip-line, .mv, .play, .segmented button, .chip, .tabbar a, summary, .text-btn and .danger, and wrap the :hover rules in @media (hover: hover). Even .btn:active is weak: scale(0.97) on a 44px button is 1.3px, animated over 120ms (app.css:131-139), so a tap of about 100ms barely shows it. button.mv:hover copies .mv.current's background and colour but not its 2px inset underline (drill:1489-1491). The stale-hover case mostly happens when the board is used next: chessground's non-passive touchstart suppresses synthetic mouse events, so hover stays on an index-keyed move button (drill:949) that now shows a different move.

results.measured: .input sets no font-size (app.css:217-226), and inputs take font: inherit (app.css:91-95) from the 15px body (app.css:62). 15 is under 16, so iOS zooms on focus. The inputs are +page.svelte:68 (first run only), settings:109 and settings:157. The zoom factor is about 16/15 = 1.067, so after a focus the 381px board renders at about 406px on a 393px screen (about 13px cropped) until the user pinches out.
results.note: The cause is certain. That the zoom persists after blur and across the SPA, and that it brings back the click delay and double-tap zoom, is plausible WebKit behaviour I can't confirm from code. It is triggered rarely (Settings and first run only) and the zoom is small, but the fix is one line: .input { font-size: 16px }.

results.measured: The code fact is right: touch-action appears only at Board.svelte:121 (none), drill:2072 (sheet backdrop, none; the audit missed this one), drill:2080-2083 (none) and drill:2085-2087 (pan-x). manipulation is not used anywhere. But the viewport is width=device-width, initial-scale=1 (app.html:5), and WebKit's fast-tap already turns off double-tap zoom at initial scale. The risk is mainly real after an accidental zoom (global-3).
results.note: Cheap insurance, as the audit says. The claim that an html-level rule can't reach buttons inside .moves/.chips holds for panning. For double-tap zoom, which belongs to the viewport, the ancestor intersection probably runs up to the root, so that part is unproven. Putting the rule on the controls themselves works either way.

results.measured: The manifest has no orientation member (static/manifest.webmanifest). Only the top and bottom safe-area insets are used (app.css:31-32). A landscape viewport of 852x393 still matches max-width: 899px, so the board becomes 852 - 12 = 840px tall in a 393px-tall viewport. Only the unprefixed text-size-adjust is set (app.css:65).
The only focus style is .input:focus (app.css:228-230); there is no :focus-visible rule. The keyboard shortcuts it would serve are at drill:705-721.

missed.title: Why sheet: Expand, Close, Next and Play form a 2x2 block with 2-6px gutters
missed.where: web/src/routes/drill/+page.svelte:1146-1156 (Expand, Close) and 1159-1183 (step arrows, Play); CSS 1949-1954 (.sheet-head gap 4px, padding 6 6 2 12), 1966-1972 (.sheet-step gap 2px, padding 2 8 6 4), 2004-2014 (.play 40x40); global .icon-btn 44x44 (app.css:156-164)
missed.evidence: openSheet sets top = board bottom 504 + 6 = 510 (drill:649-650). Head: 510 + 1px border + 6px padding gives y 517-561. Close is at x 393-6-44 = 343-387 and Expand 4px to its left at 295-339. The step row starts at 561 + 2 + 2 = 565. With no note, the next arrow is at x 393-8-40-2-44 = 299-343, y 565-609, and Play at x 345-385, y 567-607. Gutters: Expand to Close 4px, next arrow to Play 2px, Expand above the next arrow 4px, Close above Play 6px. Centre-to-centre pitch is 44-48px (7.3-7.9 mm). The sheet is fixed at z-index 20 (drill:1939) and covers the foot at z-index 2 (drill:1863). So every Why? ends with a tap on Close, or a tap on the board, which closes the sheet through an invisible backdrop that nothing signals (drill:1131). IMG_1392 confirms the sheet top at 509.7 CSS (that older build had no Expand button).
missed.fix: Put Continue inside the sheet as a full-width 48px bottom bar, so it never has to be closed first. Close it with a grabber and swipe down; the head is already touch-action: none. Drop Expand, or merge it into the drag. Give Play 12px or more from the next arrow, or turn the step controls into one equal-width toolbar [prev | Play | next] at least 48px tall, the way Chess.com does.
missed.impact: On every Why? use, the most-used target (Close) has two different actions 4-6px away: one expands the sheet over the board, the other starts autoplay. This is exactly the 'buttons really close together' complaint.

missed.title: Foot buttons change position and meaning from one result to the next
missed.where: web/src/routes/drill/+page.svelte:1091-1118 (foot branches); .actions 1683-1694; retry() 631-642
missed.evidence: Positions from .actions gap 10px, .btn flex 1 and .continue flex 1.6 in 381px. Taught move: Why? at x 6-149, Continue at 159-387. Good move, or a miss after Show answer: Try again 6-107, Why? 117-217, Continue 227-387 (Try again's min-content is about 101). Miss: Try again (primary, blue) 6-191.5, Show answer 201.5-387. So the x 6-107 spot that is Why? on most cards is Try again after a Good move, and retry() clears the result and the review. x 159-217 is Continue on one card and Why? on the next. The bottom-right spot, Continue on every answered card, is the Show answer spoiler after a miss. The blue primary button jumps from the right to the left. The 4:57 PM screenshot shows the three-button state at y 760-803.5 with widths 106/106/148; at that moment Continue had flex 1.4. Every commit since e68a183 has 1.6, so the current widths are 101/100/160.
missed.fix: Fixed slots that don't depend on state: [secondary left | Why? | primary right]. Continue always takes the right slot at the same width. After a miss, put Try again (the forward action) in that right slot and Show answer on the left. When there is no Try again, leave its slot empty instead of reflowing.
missed.impact: Fast, position-based tapping (the normal rhythm of a drill) hits a different action than intended, such as retrying instead of opening Why?, or revealing the answer instead of continuing.

missed.title: Step arrows never disable at the ends, so a no-op tap looks like a miss
missed.where: web/src/routes/drill/+page.svelte:939, 965 (move row arrows), 1160, 1179 (sheet arrows); browse() 446-456; app.css:171-173 (.icon-btn:disabled already styled); compare explore/+page.svelte:129-142
missed.evidence: None of the four arrows has a disabled attribute; the only disabled controls are the two Play buttons (drill:971, 1180). browse() clamps instead (drill:451-455), so these taps change nothing: prev at move 0, next on the drill position while asking (cursor = min(end, cursor+1)), and next on a line's last move. The buttons stay at full opacity as bare 34x34 glyphs. The tap highlight is off (app.css:64) and .icon-btn has no :active, so a no-op tap looks exactly like a 1px miss.
missed.fix: Add disabled={!canStep(-1)} and disabled={!canStep(1)} using the same clamps as browse(). Keep .icon-btn:disabled { opacity: .35 }. Optionally fire a light haptic only on real steps.
missed.impact: The user re-aims and taps again, more carefully, at a target that has nothing left to do. That feeds the feeling of 'you need to be precise'.

missed.title: Half-visible moves and chips at the scroller edges sit 2px from the arrows
missed.where: web/src/routes/drill/+page.svelte:1321-1327 (.chips), 1439-1448 (.moves), 1400-1405 (navrow gap 2px); centring effects 736-749
missed.evidence: In the result phase the move scroller spans x 42-266 (381-34-2-2-34-2-4-79 = 224) and the next arrow starts at x 268. Neither .moves nor .chips has scroll-snap, scroll-padding or an edge fade; Explore has a fade (explore:306). In the 5:02 PM screenshot, '5.Be' is cut off at the scroller edge (CSS x 229-266), 2px from the next arrow (268-302): a sliver of one target right beside a different one. The centring effect keeps the current move mid-row, which usually leaves partial items at both ends.
missed.fix: On .moves and .chips, add mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, transparent, #000 12px, #000 calc(100% - 12px), transparent) and scroll-padding-inline: 12px. Add scroll-snap-type: x proximity with scroll-snap-align: center on .mv and .chip-line. Keep at least 8px between the scroller and the arrows.
missed.impact: A tap aimed at the half-visible move near x 262-270 can step the board instead, or the reverse. The clipped item also looks like a full target.

missed.title: The move row drops 44px and the next arrow jumps 85px left when the answer lands
missed.where: web/src/routes/drill/+page.svelte:907 (chip row only in the result phase), 966-979 (Play only in the result phase), 1400-1428
missed.evidence: Before answering there is no chip row and no Play button. The move row sits at y 512-546, the next arrow at x 353-387, and the move scroller is 309px wide. When the result appears, the chip row (36 + 8px gap) pushes the move row down to y 556-594. Play (79px + 4px margin) takes x 308-387, the next arrow moves to x 268-302, and the scroller shrinks to 224px. The spot where the next arrow was while asking is now Play, 44px lower. The row height also changes from 34 to 38.
missed.fix: Keep the same layout in every phase. Reserve the chip row and the Play slot while asking (empty or disabled; there's room, since the ask screen ends about 50px short of the bottom). Or move prev / Play / next into a fixed toolbar.
missed.impact: Muscle memory from stepping through the game before answering lands on Play, or on nothing, right after answering.

missed.title: After a deploy the app reloads itself a few seconds after launch, while the user may be mid-tap
missed.where: web/src/service-worker.ts:16-32 (skipWaiting at :21, clients.claim at :30); web/src/routes/+layout.svelte:45-50 (controllerchange calls location.reload())
missed.evidence: The app shell is served cache-first (service-worker.ts:43-53), so after a deploy the old version opens instantly. The navigation's update check then installs the new worker, which caches every build and static file first: about 0.6 MB of build output plus 2.8 MB of static files, including the 1.8 MB Stockfish wasm and the 0.5 MB explanations.json. It then calls skipWaiting() and clients.claim(), the layout sees controllerchange, and the page reloads. That lands seconds after a cold launch, typically while the user is already tapping the Drill card or answering the first card. The reload restarts the session with a new deck (start()). The user deploys many times a day (12 commits on Nov 10).
missed.fix: On controllerchange, set an updateReady flag and reload only at a safe point: on the Home route, or in load() between cards. Or show a small 'New version, Reload' chip. Alternatively, drop skipWaiting so the new worker takes over at the next cold launch.
missed.impact: The page changes under a tap that's already on its way, and the drill restarts. From the user's side it looks like an unexplained mis-tap.

results.measured: Segment height is 32px (app.css:184), width is label + 28. I measured the labels myself with JXA/NSString and got the audit's numbers: All 17.3+28=45.3, White 67.3, Black 64.9; 3 mo 61.5, 6 mo 61.7, 1 yr 51.9, 2 yr 53.8, All 45.3; 2x 45.7, 3x 46.0, 5x 45.9, 10x 53.0; Slow 60.3, Normal 76.9, Fast 56.5; By need 82.3, Random 83.4; On 47.2, Off 49.5. Track is 3+32+3 = 38px tall. Period track is 3+274.2+4x2+3 = 288.2px. Dead area = 1 - (274.2x32)/(288.2x38) = 1 - 8774/10952 = 19.9%. Device check on IMG_1388: at de9fafb the drill sheet used the global .segmented with no scoped override (only one 'segmented' match in that file). At x=560 the track spans y 2251-2364 = 114 device px = 38 CSS. At x=500 the selected segment spans y 2260-2355 = 96 px = 32 CSS. The left rim is x 190-198 = 9 px = 3 CSS. Contrast: selected #15171c vs track #1c1f26 = 1.09:1. Labels #e9eaee vs #a3a8b3 = 1.98:1.
results.note: Two corrections. (1) The selected #15171c only equals the background in the drill sheet, where the photo was taken. On Mistakes, Lines and Settings the control sits on the page, #0d0e11. The selected segment is 1.08:1 against that, and the track itself is only 1.17:1. So the conclusion holds, and the whole control is nearly invisible. (2) iOS probably will not snap rim or seam taps to a neighbour. Svelte 5 puts its delegated click listener on the app root, so WebKit always finds a click-responding ancestor and skips its near-miss search (see missed secondary-v1). Rim and seam taps just do nothing. Bench sizes by my measurement: '12' 15.4+28 = 43.4, '1' 6.8+28 = 34.8 (developer only).

results.measured: Each crumb is 6+21.75+6 = 33.75px tall (15px x 1.45; explore:312). Widths are label + 18: Start 35.6+18 = 53.6, 1.e4 47.6, e5 36.1, 2.Nf3 58.1, Nc6 47.3, 3.Bb5 60.5, a6 36.2. Together that is 339.4 + 6 gaps x 2 = 351.4 of 361px. The 7th move (4.Ba4, 60.4) starts at x 353.4. That is inside the faded band (0.08 x 361 = 28.9px, from x 332) and mostly past the edge. Gap is 2px (explore:302 crumbs, :412 mainline). grep finds no scrollIntoView or scrollLeft anywhere in src. Every crumb tap calls goto without replaceState (explore:83).
results.note: Two additions. The current-crumb marker is var(--bg-elev-2) #1c1f26 on #0d0e11, only 1.17:1, so even when the current crumb is on screen it is hard to spot. The 'Start' crumb (x 16-69.6, 2px from '1.e4') runs the same go([]) as the Start button, so there are two one-slip ways to wipe the line.

results.measured: Controls are 4x44 + 3x6 = 194px wide. (361-194)/2 = 83.5, so x = 99.5-143.5, 149.5-193.5, 199.5-243.5, 249.5-293.5. Vertically, y = 75 + 24 (title min-height; baseline stack 16.23+7.45 = 23.7) + 10 + 361 + 10 = 480 to 524. .icon-btn has no fill or border; only :hover paints one (app.css:156-169). In explore:81-84 and :129-143: Start = go([]), Back = go(ucis.slice(0,-1)) (drops the move), Forward = node.moves[0] (not redo). Manifest is display: standalone.
results.note: Also, only 10px separates the board's bottom rank (y 424.9-470) from the buttons. A high tap on Back can select a rank-1 piece, or play a rank-1 move if a piece is already selected. A low tap on rank 1 can hit Back. The fix should add space here too. The icons 'first' and 'chevron-left' are near-identical 20px glyphs.

results.measured: Layout from the top: title 75-99, board 109-470, controls 480-524, panel starts at 540. Crumbs take 35.75 (to 575.75), then 14 gap. Reach block at 589.75: 43.5 + 10 + 21.75 + 10 + 8 = 93.25 (to 683). Then 14 + 6 margin, heading 703-721.85, then 14 gap. First row is 735.85-779.05. The tab bar top is 852-92 = 760, so 24.15px of row 1 is visible. This only holds when the games count has 2 or more digits. With '37': 36.6+10+316.1 = 362.7 > 361, so the reach text wraps. With a 1-digit count: 19.2+10+316.1 = 345.3, no wrap, everything moves up 31.75, and row 1 sits fully visible at 704-747. touch-action:none is confirmed (Board.svelte:121). chessground's pieceCloseTo radius is bounds.width/8 = 45.1px (drag.js:70-77). In the start position only the band from mid-rank 3 to mid-rank 6 (3 squares = 135px = 37%) is more than one square from every piece.
results.note: Three overstatements. (1) The touch-action:auto fix would free only about a quarter to a third of the board in opening positions, not most of it. The pinned-board fix is the one that matters. (2) 'The board is off screen' is too strong. Getting 4 rows (to y 908.8) above 760 takes 149px of scroll, which moves the board to -40..321. That hides about the top 2.2 ranks. The whole board only goes when you reach the continuation chips (doc y ~900+). (3) In the sticky fix, padding-top: var(--safe-t) on .board-col also applies at scroll 0 (75+59). Main's top padding has to drop to match.

results.measured: .danger is 6+21.75+6 = 33.75px tall (settings:328-333, 15px x 1.45). Reset is 138.8px wide and 245.3 once armed. Clear is 139.2 and 256.7 armed. align-self:flex-start means the armed label grows rightwards from the same left edge, so the first tap point stays inside it. confirmReset and confirmClear have no timeout (settings:50-61, 94-101). Disconnect is 80.8+36 = 116.8 x 44 and calls setLichess(null) immediately (settings:45-48).
results.note: On a width=device-width page iOS sends a fast double tap as two clicks, so a double tap confirms.

results.measured: toggleClass calls applyFilter(), which runs setFilter then analyze() (state.svelte.ts:172-177). analyze() bumps the worker's run id, which cancels and restarts the analysis (data.worker.ts:101, :234). Widening the period calls sync(), and sync() returns early while app.syncing (state.svelte.ts:151), so a later tap can't cancel it. missed.title: Near-misses do nothing: iOS's tap snapping likely can't help, so every gap, seam and rim is dead
missed.where: web/node_modules/svelte/src/internal/client/render.js:231-246 (delegated listener added to the mount target and document); web/node_modules/@sveltejs/kit/src/runtime/server/page/render.js:478 (target = document.currentScript.parentElement, the display:contents div at src/app.html:18). Dead zones: app.css:177-178 (.segmented padding 3px, gap 2px), explore:290 (.controls gap 6px), explore:302 (.crumbs gap 2px), LeakCard.svelte:74-75 (gap 8px, padding 12px), settings:271 (.chips gap 8px)
missed.evidence: Svelte 5 routes every onclick through one click listener on the mount target. On iOS, WebKit finds the tapped node by walking up from the hit element to the first ancestor that responds to clicks, stopping at body. Per its FrameIOS source, it only tests nearby points when it finds no such ancestor. Here the root div always qualifies. So a tap 1px outside a button is delivered to the track, card or gap element, Svelte finds no handler, and nothing happens. Nothing snaps to the nearest control. app.css:64 makes the tap highlight transparent, which hides even that cue. The code facts are verified; the WebKit behaviour comes from its source and was not tested on a device. Dead areas on these screens: 19.9% of the Period control (288.2x38 visible, 274.2x32 live); 41% of each LeakCard (the 12px rim plus a 275.9x44 strip); 8px between chips; 2px between crumbs; 6px between Explore's step buttons. The same mechanism applies on the drill screen.
missed.fix: Make hit areas meet edge to edge and keep the visible shapes inset. Segmented: padding:0; gap:0; buttons flex:1; height:44px; border:3px solid transparent; background-clip:padding-box (a 38px visible pill with a 44px hit area). Chips: position:relative plus ::after{content:'';position:absolute;inset:-4px -4px} so neighbours touch. Crumbs: gap:0 with 8px side padding. LeakCard: move the padding into a.main. Explore controls: grid with the gaps absorbed into the buttons.
missed.impact: This is a direct cause of 'you need to be precise': a slightly-off tap is ignored instead of hitting the nearest control, so users slow down and tap again.

missed.title: Explore's rows and Forward still act on the previous position for a moment after each move
missed.where: web/src/routes/explore/+page.svelte:34-45 (node replaced only when the worker answers), :135-143 (Forward uses node.moves[0]), :174-188 (old rows combined with new ucis); web/src/lib/chess/line.ts:34, :43-46
missed.evidence: go() changes the URL, so ucis, line and yourTurn update at once. node keeps the old position until data().node() resolves. In between, the rows show sanOf(newPos, oldUci), which falls back to raw UCI such as 'g1f3' because the move is illegal for the side now to move. The heading also flips between Your moves and Their replies above the old rows. Tapping a row, or tapping Forward a second time quickly, appends the old move. walk() stops at the illegal move, so the board doesn't change, but a history entry is pushed: the tap is lost. Usually this lasts milliseconds; it is longer while the data worker is busy with a sync or analysis.
missed.fix: Store node together with its key and render rows only when that key matches the current one. Until then keep the old rows dimmed with pointer-events:none (no layout jump), and disable Forward.
missed.impact: Fast stepping through a line silently loses taps.

missed.title: Re-tapping the selected Period or Reach segment restarts the analysis
missed.where: web/src/routes/settings/+page.svelte:63-67 (setMinReach), :78-82 (setPeriod); web/src/lib/state.svelte.ts:172-177; web/src/lib/worker/data.worker.ts:101, :234
missed.evidence: Neither handler checks whether the value changed. setPeriod(current) computes widened=false, then applyFilter() runs data().setFilter and analyze(). setMinReach(current) runs analyze(). analyze() bumps the run id, which cancels and restarts the analysis, and that also triggers the layout shift in secondary-v3. results.measured: The override is at drill/+page.svelte:2137-2140, not 2138-2141. results.note: One nuance: iOS WebKit retries a missed tap with probes at (-4,-4), (-8,-8), (+4,+4) and (-12,-12) px (see missed nav-home-m2). So when a right thumb falls short, landing below or right of the X, the tap still fires within about 12px. Example: a tap at (24,109) hits through the (12,97) probe, but a tap at (24,114) does nothing. Taps that land above or left of it get at most 4px of help. Medium severity is fair to slightly high: this happens once per session, and a miss does nothing.

missed.title: iOS's built-in tap correction barely works in this app, so each small target is exactly as big as its CSS box
missed.where: web/node_modules/@sveltejs/kit/src/runtime/client/client.js:361 (container = document.documentElement), :2110, :2125-2126, :2706 (mousemove, mousedown, touchstart and click listeners on <html>); WebKit Source/WebCore/page/LocalFrame.cpp LocalFrame::qualifyingNodeAtViewportLocation, reached through nodeRespondingToClickEvents (ShouldApproximate::Yes), which WebPageIOS.mm attemptSyntheticClick uses for one-finger taps
missed.evidence: For a tap, WebKit iOS hit-tests the point and walks up to the first ancestor that responds to clicks (click/mousedown/mouseup listeners, mousemove listeners, links, focusable elements). If there is no such ancestor, it tries 12 nearby points (±4 and ±8px diagonals, ±14px straight out) and picks the clickable element that overlaps best. The radius is int(15 x ppiFactor), with ppiFactor = (460/3)/163 = 0.94, giving 14. That's the normal fat-finger help. Here SvelteKit puts click and mousedown listeners on <html>, so <html> always qualifies. WebKit then only runs a 4-point refinement at (-4,-4), (-8,-8), (+4,+4) and (-12,-12), in that order. The result: misses that land right of or below a target get up to about 12px of help, misses above or left get at most 4px, and the gap between two targets goes to the upper or left one. Drill footer example (Screenshot 4.57.09 PM: Try again x 6–112.3, Why? 122.3–228.7, Continue 239–386.7, y 760–804): about 8px of each 10px gap goes to the left button, so a tap just left of Continue opens Why?. On home, the whole 8px gap above LeakCard's Drill button goes to the explorer link.
missed.impact: This is the platform reason the app feels like it needs precise taps. The 15–37px text links (All, All N, Connect Lichess, Got it) and the 36px drill X get no forgiveness for misses above or left, and gaps between buttons quietly belong to the left or upper neighbour.
missed.fix: Build hit areas into the CSS instead of relying on the browser. Give small controls invisible hit slop (`position: relative` plus `::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -8px }`) so each is at least 44x44. Between adjacent buttons, either use gaps of 12px or more, or extend each button's ::after into the gap (`inset: 0 -5px` in a 10px gap) so the hit areas meet at the midline and a gap tap goes to the nearer button. Leave SvelteKit's root listeners alone; routing needs them.

touch-accuracy.topic: Touch-target size, spacing and precision on phones (converted to iPhone 15 Pro points), and design patterns for screens dense with controls, applied to the chess-trainer drill UI (/Users/jwahbeh/chess-trainer/web)

findings.claim: Apple's iOS baseline is unchanged: a 44×44 pt hit region, with 28×28 pt as the absolute minimum. Apple also now says spacing matters as much as size: about 12 pt of padding around controls with a bezel, and about 24 pt around the visible edges of controls without one (text- or icon-only).
findings.detail: Accessibility table: iOS/iPadOS default 44×44 pt, minimum 28×28 pt (visionOS 60/28, tvOS 66/56, watchOS 44/28). Quote: 'Consider spacing between controls as important as size. Include enough padding between elements to reduce the chance that someone taps the wrong control.' Buttons page: 'a button needs a hit region of at least 44x44 pt'. For visionOS: button centres at least 60 pt apart, and avoid rows or stacks of small/mini buttons. The accessibility guidance was expanded on 7 Mar 2025 (page last changed 9 Jun 2025). The iOS 26 / Liquid Glass revisions (9 Jun and 16 Dec 2025) did not change any sizes.

findings.claim: The iOS 26 (Liquid Glass) HIG changes are about grouping and hierarchy, not size. Group bar items by function and frequency; use at most about three groups; put fixed space between text-labelled buttons; have exactly one tinted primary action, on the trailing side; and use a More menu for less important actions.
findings.detail: Toolbars page (9 Jun 2025: 'Added guidance for grouping bar items'): 'Group toolbar items logically by function and frequency of use'; 'Minimize the number of groups… aim for a maximum of three'; 'Keep actions with text labels separate… inserting fixed space'; 'Only specify one primary action, and put it on the trailing side'; 'Choose items deliberately to avoid overcrowding. People need to be able to distinguish and activate each item'. WWDC25 'Get to know the new design system': 'Group bar items by function and frequency'; 'If your bar is feeling too crowded… move secondary actions into a more menu'. iOS also moved Search into a bottom tab, 'easier to reach'. Buttons page: 'Keep the number of prominent buttons to one or two per view', and never give a destructive action the primary role.

findings.claim: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA) is only a floor: 24×24 CSS px, or smaller if a 24 px circle centred on each target doesn't touch another target or circle. SC 2.5.5 (AAA) is 44×44 CSS px. W3C itself says touch research points to larger sizes, and that 24 px was chosen because the rule has to work for every pointer type.
findings.detail: 2.5.8 exceptions: Spacing, Equivalent, Inline (in a sentence or limited by line-height), User-agent control, Essential. Understanding doc: 'Requiring large, touch-optimized minimum sizes would not have been appropriate as a threshold for all pointer inputs'. It encourages authors to go beyond the minimum and to use 2.5.5 for important controls. 2.5.5's benefit list names touchscreen use, one-handed use and shaking environments. Note: inline text links pass 2.5.8 through the Inline exception even though they are physically tiny.

findings.claim: Google/Material: 48×48 dp targets, at least 8 dp apart. Google equates 48 dp with 'about 9 mm' and recommends 7–10 mm physical. Compose automatically extends a small control's touch target beyond its drawn bounds to 48 dp. web.dev gives the same 48 px / 8 px rule for the web. Lighthouse flags a target under 48×48 px when more than 25% of the 48 px area around its centre overlaps another target.
findings.detail: Caution: on an iPhone 15 Pro, 48 CSS px is 7.95 mm, not 9 mm; about 54 pt is needed for 9 mm. Hoober notes that 48 dp renders up to about 30% smaller or larger across Android devices. web.dev's example: a 24 px icon padded out to a 48 px target, and more link padding under @media (any-pointer: coarse).

findings.claim: Microsoft sizes targets by what a wrong tap costs. 7×7 mm if the mistake is fixed in 1–2 gestures or 5 s. 9×9 mm when accuracy matters (close, delete, or recovery that takes more than 2 gestures, more than 5 s, or a context change). 5×5 mm only when a mis-tap is fixed in one gesture and there is 2 mm of padding. Quote: 'Padding between targets is just as important as target size.'
findings.detail: Windows 7/8 touch guide: at least 6×6 mm for efficient, accurate finger use; 10×10 mm 'enables better speed and accuracy, and also feels more comfortable'. Make click targets larger than the visible element. Controls placed close together but not touching lead to taps on 'inactive space' with no feedback, so users can't tell what went wrong. 'Have clear physical separation between frequently used commands and destructive commands.' Give feedback on finger-down but act on finger-up, and let users slide off to correct. Current WinUI guidance: 7.5 mm by default; make frequently pressed targets larger; give severe-consequence targets more padding and keep them further from the edge of the content area.

findings.claim: People don't hold phones one way. In 1,333 street observations (780 people touching the screen), 49% used one hand, 36% cradled the phone, and 15% used two hands, and grips changed 'sometimes every few seconds'. Later work found about 75% tap with one thumb, and that people prefer to look at and tap the centre of the screen, where they are fastest and most accurate.
findings.detail: In a 2017 update Hoober asked readers to disregard his 2013 reach heat-maps: the centre, not a 'thumb zone', is the sweet spot. People 'almost always tap the center two-thirds of the screen' (2014). He recommends key content and actions in the middle half to two-thirds, secondary options along the top and bottom, and no dangerous functions where a shifting grip makes accidental taps likely. This supports the user's own view: thumb reach is secondary to size and spacing.

findings.claim: Accuracy varies by screen region. A target that catches 95% of taps can be about 7 mm in the centre, but needs about 9–10 mm along the left and right edges, about 11 mm at the top, and about 12 mm at the bottom and in the corners.
findings.detail: Hoober 2017: 'Accuracy varies from 7 mm at the center of the screen to 12 mm at the corners'. Rows along the left/right edges should be at least 9–10 mm tall. Used one-handed while carrying a bag, the far corner can exceed 30 mm. Design about 20% larger for poor conditions, and limit top or bottom action bars to about 4 items on iOS (5 on the largest phones). 4ourth (2022): centre 7 / edges 9 / corners 12 mm. The book figures (top 11 mm, bottom 12 mm, centre 7 mm) come via Smashing, a secondary source, so treat top/bottom as medium confidence. Smashing's px conversions (42/46/27 px) assume 96 px per inch and are about 37% too small for an iPhone. On iPhone 15 Pro: 7 mm = 42 pt, 9 mm = 54 pt, 11 mm = 66 pt, 12 mm = 72 pt.

findings.claim: Interference (a tap meant for one target landing on its neighbour) is the most serious touch error. Hoober's rule is at least 8 mm centre-to-centre between targets (10 mm preferred), with touch targets 6 mm minimum, 8 mm preferred, 15 mm maximum (2013).
findings.detail: To check a layout, overlay an 8 mm inner and a 10 mm outer circle on each target, on a real screen or a scaled screenshot. If neighbours' circles overlap, spacing is too tight. Spacing is measured centre-to-centre, so drawn size doesn't matter for this check. On iPhone 15 Pro, an 8 mm pitch is 48 pt and 10 mm is 60 pt.

findings.claim: Parhi, Karlson & Bederson (MobileHCI 2006), one-handed thumb use: errors stopped improving at 9.6 mm and up for single taps, and at 7.7 mm and up for keypad-style serial taps. They recommend 9.2 mm for discrete taps and 9.6 mm for serial taps.
findings.detail: 20 right-handed participants on an HP iPAQ h4155 (3.5-inch screen). Discrete targets were 3.8–11.5 mm, surrounded by distractors, and selected on thumb lift-off. Serial keypad keys were 5.8–13.4 mm with 0 mm gaps. Errors at 3.8 and 5.8 mm were significantly higher than at all other sizes, and 7.7 mm had more errors than 11.5 mm. For 9.6 mm targets, a 9.1×8.9 mm box enclosed 95% of hits at any screen location. Location had no significant effect on errors, but corners had wider hit spread, the centre was rated most comfortable (5.7/7), and users wanted the largest targets in the NW, SW and SE corners. NN/g turns this into a 1×1 cm minimum.

findings.claim: Fingers are much bigger than typical controls. The widely cited MIT Touch Lab figure is a 16–20 mm average adult index-finger width, with a thumb contact area of about 25 mm. MacKenzie measured index-finger width at 14.0 mm (SD 1.4).
findings.detail: NN/g (Harley, 2019) and Smashing (2012) cite 16–20 mm. Scott Hurff summarises the same lab as finger pad 10–14 mm and fingertip 8–10 mm. The secondary sources disagree and I couldn't retrieve the primary MIT PDF (expired certificate), so treat these as order-of-magnitude figures. NN/g: 'the fat fingers are not the real culprit; the blame should lie on the tiny targets', and if targets are too small, 'adding space between them is likely not going to help'.

findings.claim: Fitts's law under-predicts how hard small touch targets are, because a finger has a fixed imprecision that slowing down can't remove (Bi, Li & Zhai, Google, CHI 2013, 'FFitts law'). The touch-point SD measured in their 2D calibration was about 1.5 mm.
findings.detail: In their 2D tasks the effective width (4.133 × the SD of taps) stayed around 6.9–8.2 mm whatever the target size. Error rates were about 65–66% for 2.4 mm targets, 25–27% for 4.8 mm and about 7% for 7.2 mm (1D: 29–38%, 11–14%, 3–6%). Below about 8 mm, misses are built in; users can only make up for it by slowing down and aiming, which is the 'you need to be precise' feeling.

findings.claim: Touch is fast but imprecise. On a Nexus 4, 6.2 mm targets had 12.2% errors versus 2.7% for about 10.3 mm targets, while throughput was a high 6.95 bits/s, against 3.7–4.9 for a mouse (MacKenzie, HCII 2015).
findings.detail: 16 participants, index finger. The 10.3 mm figure is my calculation from 130 px at the paper's stated scale; the paper gives 78 px = 6.2 mm. Finger width averaged 14 mm, more than twice the small target.

findings.claim: Henze, Rukzio & Boll's in-the-wild data (MobileHCI 2011; 91,731 installs, about 120 M touches from an Android game) showed that error rates depend on target size and screen position, and that touch positions are systematically skewed. A compensation function cut errors by 7.79% in a follow-up with about 15 M touches.
findings.detail: Per Hoober's and Hurff's summaries: errors rise sharply below about 12–15 mm and exceed 40% for targets under 8 mm. Those are fast-game conditions, so the absolute rates are pessimistic. Edges are worse than the centre, roughly symmetrically. I couldn't retrieve the primary paper, so the direction of the skew is unverified. A web app can't apply per-device offset correction, so the practical answer is bigger targets and more room.

findings.claim: Much of the 'fat finger' error is really systematic offset. Holz & Baudisch (CHI 2010) found finger posture and individual user explain 67% of touch inaccuracy. Without correction, a round button had to be 15 mm across to catch 95% of touches; with per-user, per-posture correction, 5.4 mm. The cause: users aim with the top of the finger while screens sense its underside (CHI 2011: offsets of 4 mm versus 1.6 mm).
findings.detail: Earlier minimum sizes they cite: 10.5 mm (Vogel & Baudisch), 11.5 mm (Wang & Ren), 26 mm (Hall et al., tabletop). Their 15 mm figure comes from deliberately varied finger angles, so it's a worst case.

findings.claim: Real-world conditions raise the size needed. Walking raised thumb error rate by 23%, selection time by 31% and workload by 24%. Targets 20% bigger helped significantly, and 40% bigger almost fully made up for walking (Schildbach & Rukzio, MobileHCI 2010).
findings.detail: Targets of 6.74, 8.18 and 9.50 mm; 16 participants; one-handed thumb. The authors note that the iPhone's minimum target of the time (6.74 mm) gave error rates of about 23% while walking.

findings.claim: Once targets are big, extra gap adds little; size dominates. Colle & Hiszem (Ergonomics 2004) tested 10–25 mm keys with 1 or 3 mm gaps: 'spacing had no measurable effects', and 20 mm was enough. Sesto et al. (Human Factors 2012; 52 users, including people with motor disabilities) tested 10–30 mm buttons with 1 or 3 mm gaps: size changed touch behaviour, spacing didn't. Spacing does matter when targets are small (Microsoft's 5 mm + 2 mm rule; Apple's 12/24 pt padding).
findings.detail: My synthesis (medium confidence): what matters is each target's hit area and the centre-to-centre pitch. When space is short, give it to hit area (hit regions that touch, with the visuals kept apart) rather than to empty gaps. Microsoft notes that taps landing in empty gaps do nothing and give no feedback.

findings.claim: Dense, costly neighbours make people slow down and aim away. When tapping a neighbour has a penalty, users shift their taps away from it into empty space, and Fitts/FFitts stop predicting performance (Yamanaka, MobileHCI 2018). When the touchable area is bigger than what's drawn, users still aim cautiously at the visible element (Usuba, Yamanaka & Miyashita, MobileHCI 2019).
findings.detail: Implication: invisible hit-slop cuts misses, but the 'I have to be precise' feeling only goes away if the visible shape (pill or background) is also large and clearly separated. A NordiCHI 2018 desktop-pointing study found visually tiny targets with larger clickable areas were used 'without any problems' in time or errors, so adding hit-slop is safe.

findings.claim: Near screen edges, taps skew toward the edge (within about 6–6.7 mm). Targets that run all the way to the edge are hit more reliably than predicted, because users can tap target and bezel together (Kasahara, Yamanaka & Miyashita, arXiv, March 2026).
findings.detail: Pixel 6a, index finger; tested the left and bottom edges and the top-right corner. The authors recommend edge-adjacent targets touch the boundary (zero margin), with the caveat that thick cases or raised bezels may change this. Henze and Hoober report edges as less accurate when targets sit away from the edge. So either extend hit areas to the edge, or keep small targets away from it.

findings.claim: The finger hides small targets and their feedback. Vogel & Baudisch's Shift (CHI 2007) traces finger errors mainly to occlusion plus doubt about which part of the finger counts. Its fix, used only for small targets, is a callout above the finger plus selection on lift-off. Potter, Weldon & Shneiderman (CHI 1988) found that continuous feedback until the finger lifts produced fewer errors.
findings.detail: Hoober: 'Fingers are opaque'; make feedback big enough to see around the finger. Lichess's mobile app, by default, magnifies the dragged piece 2× and lifts it one square up (magnifyDraggedPiece=true → dragFeedbackScale 2.0, offset (0,-1)), and draws a circle around the target square under the finger (dragTargetKind=circle). Chessground web, which this app uses, shows only an origin ghost and move-dest dots, with no highlight of the square under the finger.

findings.claim: iPhone 15 Pro conversion: 1179 px ÷ 460 ppi = 65.1 mm across 393 CSS px, so 1 pt (= 1 CSS px) = 0.1657 mm and 1 mm = 6.04 pt. That makes 7 mm = 42 pt, 9 mm = 54 pt, 10 mm = 60 pt and 12 mm = 72 pt; Apple's 44 pt = 7.3 mm, Material's 48 = 7.95 mm and WCAG's 24 = 4.0 mm.
findings.source: Computed from Apple's iPhone 15 Pro specs (2556×1179 px, 460 ppi; DPR 3): https://support.apple.com/en-us/111829
findings.detail: The same scale applies to other 460 ppi @3x iPhone Pro screens. Desktop-based conversions (1 CSS px = 1/96 in = 0.265 mm), such as '11 mm ≈ 42 px', undersize phone targets by about 37%; on an iPhone, 11 mm is 66 pt.

findings.claim: The drill screen's densest row falls below every evidence-based threshold. ◀/▶ are 34×34 pt (5.6 mm) with 2 pt (0.3 mm) gaps to the move chips. Move chips are about 30 pt tall (4.9 mm) and 28–37 pt wide with 1 pt gaps, a centre-to-centre pitch of about 29–38 pt (4.8–6.3 mm) against Hoober's 48–60 pt. The '⋯' menu is about 34×28 pt. Inline text buttons ('show it', 'Back to the position', the engine-line toggle) are about 20 pt tall (3.4 mm).
findings.source: /Users/jwahbeh/chess-trainer/web/src/routes/drill/+page.svelte (.navrow/.icon-btn/.play/.moves/.mv CSS ~lines 1401–1461, .text-btn ~1841, .menu summary ~1890, markup 938–980 and 1091–1117); /Users/jwahbeh/chess-trainer/web/src/app.css (.btn/.icon-btn 122–172; body 15px/1.45); Tappy model https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.03097
findings.detail: Tappy's dual-Gaussian model (built from crowdsourced phone taps, centre of screen, no neighbour, edge or thumb effects, so optimistic) predicts per-tap success of about 94% at 34×34 pt (about a 71% chance of at least one miss in 20 stepping taps), 91–93% for move chips, 85% for '⋯' and 82% for 20 pt-tall links. Compare 98.4% at 44 pt, 99.0% at 48, 99.5% at 54 and 99.8% at 60 (about a 5% chance of a miss in 20 taps). In the nav row a miss doesn't land on nothing: it hits the next chip or arrow and shows the wrong move. The strip also auto-scrolls to the current move, so chips can move under a finger (web.dev CLS: shifts make users 'click the wrong link or button'). Two slip risks: the primary button swaps sides between states (wrong state: Try again on the left, Show answer on the right; result state: Continue on the right), so a habitual right-side tap for Continue hits 'Show answer'. And 'stop drilling this' (skipForGood) has no undo. What works: .btn/.icon-btn default to 44 pt; footer buttons are 44 pt tall with 10 pt gaps; line chips are 36 pt with 5–6 pt gaps; board squares are about 47.6 pt (7.9 mm) in the centre of the screen.

findings.claim: Hiding things in a menu costs usage, so only rare actions belong in an overflow. NN/g found hidden navigation was used in 57% of mobile cases versus 86% for 'combo' navigation (some items visible, the rest collapsed), with more than 20% lower discoverability and 15% slower tasks on mobile.
findings.detail: NN/g recommends combo navigation: keep the most important options visible and collapse the rest. Apple: 'Try to include all actions in the toolbar if possible, and only add this menu if you really need it.'

findings.claim: Prefer undo to confirmation for frequent or mis-tap-prone actions. Confirmations become habit and get clicked through (Raskin, 'Never use a warning when you mean undo', 2007). NN/g keeps confirmation dialogs for serious, irreversible actions, with buttons that name the outcome ('Delete file' / 'Keep file'), and urges undo wherever possible.
findings.detail: Microsoft's touch 'forgiveness' rests on undo, good feedback and physical separation of destructive commands. It allows touch-only routine confirmations only for actions people often trigger by accident with touch. Apple: undo 'can also help people explore and experiment safely'.

findings.claim: Keep consequential actions physically away from frequent ones. NN/g ('Dangerous UX: Consequential Options Close to Benign Options', 2021): confirmatory and destructive actions should be far apart, with extra space and redundant visual signals, and it's fine to make the consequential option a little harder to select.
findings.detail: Others agree. Microsoft: separate frequent and destructive commands; severe-consequence targets get 9 mm and more padding. Hoober: put dangerous or unrelated items far from others, and keep unrecoverable actions away from frequently used controls. Apple: never give a destructive action the primary or prominent role.

findings.claim: Gestures are good accelerators for stepping, but they must add to visible buttons, not replace them. Apple requires custom gestures to be discoverable and 'not the only way to perform an important action'. Microsoft names 'scrubbing' (sliding a finger across small, dense elements) as the touch way to choose among them. Chess.com's Game Review lets you swipe across the move list to go faster. Lichess's mobile app repeats ◀/▶ on long-press, speeding up (200→180→100→40 ms, then every 30 ms). iOS UIStepper repeats on hold by default.

Prominence works. In Google's M3 Expressive research (46 studies, 18,000+ participants, I/O 2025), participants spotted key UI elements up to 4× faster. In the email case study, the Send button was enlarged, given a high-contrast container, and moved out of the top toolbar to just above the keyboard.
findings.detail: Google credits larger buttons and high-contrast containers with better usability for people with a range of motor and visual abilities, and says tap times for key actions dropped 'by seconds'. This is vendor research with few method details.

findings.claim: On iOS Safari, double-tap-to-zoom can get in the way of rapid repeated taps, such as stepping with ◀▶. Setting `touch-action: manipulation` on an element makes WebKit ignore double-taps there and fire single taps immediately. With width=device-width, fast single taps are only guaranteed at the initial zoom scale.
findings.detail: WebKit (Dec 2015): a 350 ms delay before single taps when a double-tap zoom is possible. This app's viewport is 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover', which still allows zoom. In the drill page only the board, the sheet backdrop and the sheet rows set touch-action; .navrow and .foot do not.

findings.claim: Chess.com's app keeps controls few and big. Game Review has a bottom bar of three actions (Show, Best, Retry) plus one green Next as the primary, with arrows either side of the move list and swipe on the list. Game Analysis puts back/forward arrows at the bottom of the screen and folds rare actions (reset, flip, share, continue against a bot) into one 'Options' menu, with display toggles behind a cog.
