patterns.name: Hit area bigger than the visual (hit-slop), with no dead gaps
patterns.description: Give every target a touch region of at least 44×44 pt whatever its drawn size. Do it with padding on the element itself, or a position:relative parent plus ::after{content:'';position:absolute;inset:-8px} (or inset:0 to make a whole row or card tappable). Split the space between neighbours so hit regions touch, each taking half the gap: no dead zones (taps there do nothing and give no feedback) and no overlaps (check with WCAG 24 px circles or Lighthouse's 25% overlap rule). Pseudo-element slop is clipped by overflow:auto/hidden ancestors, and a horizontal scroller clips in both directions. Inside a scrolling strip, make the element itself taller and draw a smaller pill inside it. Users aim at what they see (Usuba 2019), so pair invisible slop with a visible pressed or pill shape close to the real hit size.
patterns.applyHere: ◀/▶ in .navrow: grow the hit area from 34 to at least 44 pt, ideally 48–54 pt wide, keeping the 18 px glyph. Move chips (.mv): min-height and min-width 44 pt, a ~30 pt visual pill centred inside, and gap 0 so hit areas touch. They sit in the overflow-x:auto .moves strip, so use padding rather than ::after. '⋯' summary: 44×44. Text buttons ('show it', 'Back to the position', the engine-line toggle): vertical padding up to 44 pt with a matching negative margin, or turn them into real buttons. Add :active backgrounds to .icon-btn and .mv; they only style :hover, which doesn't fire on touch.
patterns.seenIn: Material/Compose automatic touch-target expansion and minimumInteractiveComponentSize; Windows (16 px icon → 23 px target; text rows 8 px wider than the text); web.dev (24 px icon padded to 48 px); React Native hitSlop; Ahmad Shadeed's ::after technique; Apple's 44 pt hit region

patterns.name: Size first, then centre-to-centre pitch
patterns.description: Set sizes by the cost of a miss and by screen region. Anything tappable: at least 44 pt of hit area. Frequent or repeated controls, and anything on the top or bottom edge: 54–60 pt (9–10 mm) in at least the tight dimension, rising to 66–72 pt (11–12 mm) at the bottom edge once the bar's own padding is counted. Keep at least 48 pt (8 mm) centre-to-centre between independent targets, 60 pt (10 mm) preferred. Go down to ~30 pt (5 mm) only for controls whose mis-tap is undone in one tap, and then leave at least 12 pt (2 mm) of gap. Once hit areas reach 9–10 mm, extra gap buys little (Colle & Hiszem; Sesto).
patterns.applyHere: The move strip's pitch is about 29–38 pt today. With 44 pt chips it becomes at least 44 pt, and showing a window of moves around the current one (with '…' to expand) keeps the pitch at 48 pt or more without a wider screen. The worst spot is ◀ next to the first chip (~34 pt pitch): either give ◀/▶ at least 12 pt of clearance from the chips or move them out of the row (see the bottom-bar pattern). Footer buttons are fine at 44 × ~110 pt with a 10 pt gap; raising the primary to 52–56 pt tall fits Hoober's bottom-edge numbers.
patterns.seenIn: Hoober's 8/10 mm circles; Microsoft's 5/7/9 mm-by-consequence rule; Apple's 12/24 pt padding; Parhi's 9.2/9.6 mm

patterns.name: Group by function and frequency; separate the groups clearly
patterns.description: Cluster related controls (navigation, content, actions) into at most three groups per bar. Separate groups by 12–24 pt or a divider. Keep text-labelled buttons visibly apart from icon buttons (fixed space) so neighbours don't read as one control. Use abutting segmented groups, each segment at least 44 pt, for sets of the same kind. Extra spacing between similar items within a group also helps tell them apart.
patterns.applyHere: .navrow puts navigation (◀ ▶), content (move chips) and an action (the Play pill) within 2–6 pt of each other. Split it into a step group (◀ ▶ plus Play) and the move list as its own row and scroller. Alternatively, keep the move list mid-screen and move the step group into the bottom bar. The sheet's .sheet-step row (◀, step text, ▶, Play, with 2 pt gaps) has the same problem.
patterns.seenIn: Apple HIG Toolbars, June 2025 (group by function and frequency, ≤3 groups, fixed space between text buttons); WWDC25 'Get to know the new design system'; Samsung One UI ('actionable components are grouped'); Windows 7 guide (extra spacing between groups); Chess.com Game Analysis (arrows at the bottom, Options separate)

patterns.name: One overflow menu for rare actions (combo navigation)
patterns.description: Keep frequent actions visible. Put rarely used or settings-like actions behind a single More/Options button of at least 44×44 pt, whose menu rows are full-width and 44–48 pt tall. Don't hide frequent actions: hidden items get used less (57% vs 86%) and are discovered over 20% less often.
patterns.applyHere: The '⋯' <details> menu already holds 'I play X on purpose · stop drilling this'. Make its trigger 44×44 and move it away from the Continue row, for example to the top-right of the header or with at least 24 pt of clearance. Use it for other rare items (flip board, engine-line toggle, copy PGN) instead of adding more inline text buttons. Menu rows should be full-width buttons of at least 48 pt, with the consequential item last and in red.
patterns.seenIn: Apple HIG More menu and WWDC25; Chess.com Game Analysis 'Options' (reset, flip, share, continue against a bot); NN/g combo navigation

patterns.name: One primary action per state, always in the same place
patterns.description: Each state shows exactly one visually prominent action (filled, accent colour, widest) in a sticky slot that stays put between states. Secondary actions are quiet or outlined, and destructive actions never get the primary style. When options are the same size, rank them by style, not size (Apple).
patterns.applyHere: In the drill, Continue (result) and Try again (wrong) are the primaries. Today the primary swaps sides: wrong state = [Try again (primary)][Show answer]; result state = [Try again][Why?][Continue (primary)]. A habitual tap on the right-hand button to Continue therefore lands on 'Show answer' in the wrong state. Keep the primary in one fixed slot (for example always right-most, flex 1.6) in the wrong, 'also good' and correct states.
patterns.seenIn: Apple Buttons (1–2 prominent buttons per view) and Toolbars (one primary, trailing); Chess.com Game Review's green Next at bottom-right; M3 Expressive Send button (spotted up to 4× faster)

patterns.name: Bottom action bar: at most 4 items, hit areas to the edges
patterns.description: A sticky bottom bar above the safe area, with at most about 4 equal-width items (5 on the largest phones). Each item spans the full bar height so the bar's padding is part of its hit area, and the outer items' hit areas run to the screen edges with zero margin. Taps at the bottom edge are less precise (about 12 mm for 95%), so bar items need more height than mid-screen controls. Thumb reach is a bonus here, not the main reason.
patterns.applyHere: Turn .foot into the drill's control bar, for example [◀] [▶] [Why?/Play] [Continue]. Each item 56–64 pt tall including padding; ◀ and ▶ each about 20–25% of the width (~80–95 pt, 13–16 mm). Keep the bottom padding at var(--safe-b), but let the buttons' hit areas cover the bar's 10–12 pt top and bottom padding. The board stays in the centre (the most precise zone), with the notes above the bar.
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com Game Analysis (back/forward at the bottom) and Game Review (Show/Best/Retry + Next); Hoober (≤4 items per bar on iOS); iOS 26 floating tab bar and bottom Search tab; Samsung One UI interaction area; Kasahara 2026 (edge-touching targets)

patterns.name: Distance between consequential and frequent actions
patterns.description: Put destructive, irreversible or score-affecting actions in a different group or in the overflow menu, at the opposite end from the primary, with a text label and red colour. Give them at least 9 mm targets, but never right next to the frequent action, and never the prominent style.
patterns.applyHere: 'Show answer' (which ends the attempt) sits directly beside 'Try again' and in the slot where Continue normally is. 'Stop drilling this' is one level down in '⋯', just above Continue. Options: make 'Show answer' a quieter text-style button on its own row, or put it at the far end with at least 24 pt of clearance. Keep 'stop drilling' in the overflow (good as is) and add undo.
patterns.seenIn: NN/g 'Dangerous UX' (2021); Microsoft Windows 7/8 touch guide and WinUI targeting; Hoober; Apple Buttons

patterns.name: Undo instead of confirm
patterns.description: Do the action at once and offer undo for about 5–10 s: a toast or snackbar near the bottom bar with an 'Undo' button of at least 44 pt, or a persistent Undo on the next screen. Keep confirmation dialogs for rare, serious, irreversible actions, with buttons that name the outcome.
patterns.applyHere: skipForGood() suspends the card and loads the next one with no way back; add 'Stopped drilling Nf3 · Undo' (unsuspend and put the card back in the queue). Optional idea: a mis-drop on an adjacent legal square is graded as a wrong answer, so a 'Take back (mis-tap)' within a couple of seconds that doesn't count against the card would forgive precision errors instead of demanding more precision.
patterns.seenIn: Gmail's undo (Raskin 2007); NN/g confirmation-dialog guidance; Microsoft's touch 'forgiveness'; Apple HIG Undo and redo

patterns.name: Swipe/scrub and press-and-hold instead of precise step taps
patterns.description: Keep big visible ◀/▶ buttons, then add accelerators. Long-press repeats with acceleration (Lichess: 200, 180, 100, 40 ms, then every 30 ms; UIStepper.autorepeat is on by default). A horizontal swipe on a large surface steps one move per flick, or scrubs in proportion to drag distance and commits on release. Scrubbing across a dense strip highlights the item under the finger and selects it on lift. Don't make a gesture the only way to do something, and teach it once.
patterns.applyHere: Stepping is the most frequent repeated action here. Add hold-to-repeat on ◀/▶. Add swipe-to-step either on the move strip (it's already pan-x scrollable, so a short flick steps and a drag scrolls) or on the board during the result/review phase, when it isn't expecting a move. The board uses touch-action:none, so gestures must never run while a move is expected. Set touch-action: manipulation on the step buttons so fast double taps never zoom.
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com Game Review (swipe across the move list); Lichess mobile RepeatButton; iOS UIStepper autorepeat; Windows 'scrubbing'; Apple HIG gestures (add to buttons, don't replace them)

patterns.name: Feedback the finger can't hide, and act on lift-off
patterns.description: Show a pressed state visible around the fingertip (the whole pill or row background, plus haptics). Act on release and let a slide-off cancel. When dragging onto small cells (board squares are about 7.9 mm), lift the dragged item above the finger and mark the target cell with a larger ring, so the user can see where it will drop.
patterns.applyHere: Board.svelte (chessground) shows a ghost at the origin and move-dest dots, but nothing marks the square under the finger. Add a ring around the square under the finger, and scale and offset the dragged piece (Lichess mobile: 2×, one square up); in a drill, a mis-drop is graded as a wrong answer. For buttons, add :active states to .icon-btn and .mv, and pair them with the existing haptics in src/lib/haptics.ts.
patterns.seenIn: Vogel & Baudisch, Shift (CHI 2007); Potter et al., take-off selection (CHI 1988); Lichess mobile magnifyDraggedPiece/dragTargetKind; Hoober ('fingers are opaque'); Microsoft (feedback on finger-down, act on finger-up)

patterns.name: Size by screen region
patterns.description: Size by where the target sits: about 7 mm (42 pt) in the centre; 9–10 mm (54–60 pt) at the left and right edges; about 11 mm (66 pt) at the top; about 12 mm (72 pt) at the bottom and corners, counting any padding that's part of the hit area. Keep precision-critical small targets (the board) in the centre, and put big secondary controls at the top and bottom.
patterns.applyHere: Board squares (~47.6 pt) are fine in the centre. Header buttons and the bottom bar need the larger figures. The move strip sits mid-screen, so 44 pt targets are defensible there as long as the pitch rules hold.
patterns.seenIn: Hoober (UXmatters 2017; 4ourth 2022; Touch Design for Mobile Interfaces via Smashing 2023)

patterns.name: Measure it: circles, models, a real device
patterns.description: Overlay Hoober's 8 mm and 10 mm circles (48 pt and 60 pt across on iPhone 15 Pro), or WCAG's 24 px circles, on screenshots. Outline hit regions in a debug mode. Run Lighthouse's tap-target audit and Tappy or Tap Analyzer to estimate success rates. Test one-handed and while walking on a real iPhone.
patterns.applyHere: Add a dev-only CSS flag that outlines every button's hit box and draws a 48 pt circle at each target's centre on /drill, and use Chrome device mode with Tap Analyzer. A possible acceptance bar: no target under 44 pt, at least 48 pt centre-to-centre in the step and move area, and at least 99% predicted success for frequent controls.
patterns.seenIn: Hoober 2013 circle check; Lighthouse tap targets; Tappy (LY Corp, 2024); Tap Analyzer Chrome extension

chesscom.topic: Chess.com iOS app UI, 2024–2026: where the controls sit, their sizes, move-list navigation, move feedback, explanations, board space, board/haptics/sound settings, and user complaints about mis-taps. Most layout facts were measured from Chess.com Help Center iPhone screenshots (1170 px = 390 pt, 3 px per pt) and App Store screenshots. Lichess's open-source mobile code is used as a check where Chess.com behaviour could not be confirmed.

findings.claim: Game Review on the app puts its controls in a bottom bar. Show, Best and Retry are icon-over-label buttons, and a green Next button sits in the bottom-right corner. You step through moves with arrows at both ends of a one-row move list below the board, or by swiping left or right on that list. You can drag the coach's speech bubble down if it covers the eval bar. A cog icon (top right) holds Voice, Skills, Show Coach Avatar, Show Best Moves, Eval Bar Location, Chess Engine and Strength.
findings.detail: VERIFIED from the article text and its embedded iPhone screenshots. Screen from top to bottom (390-pt-wide phone): nav bar 56 pt (back arrow, bold 'Game Review' title, cog and analysis-magnifier icons on the right). A thin horizontal eval bar 20 pt tall, white share on the left with a number like '-2.05'. A fixed coach zone about 162 pt tall: cartoon avatar about 80 pt wide on the left, white speech bubble (radius about 16 pt) on the right. The bubble shows a 24 pt class icon, a bold headline like 'Nh3 is a mistake', a dark eval chip on the right, then 1–3 lines of explanation. Next comes the board, 390×390 pt and edge to edge. About 88 pt below the board holds the move list (about 39 pt tall, chevron hit boxes about 36×39 pt at the far left and right, current move in a pill about 24 pt tall). Then the action bar and about 38 pt of home-indicator space. The start screen has one full-width green 'Start Review' button (16 pt side margins, about 55 pt tall).

findings.claim: In Game Review the big bottom-right button changes job and colour depending on how good your move was. After an inaccuracy or mistake it becomes a red 'Retry' in exactly the same rectangle as the green 'Next', and 'Next' drops into the third small slot where Retry normally sits.
findings.source: https://support.chess.com/en/articles/10328363-how-do-i-use-game-review-on-the-app (screenshots: 'c5 is an inaccuracy' vs 'Nh3 is a mistake' / 'a3 is best')
findings.detail: VERIFIED by pixel measurement: the red Retry (#E02828, darker lip #9D1C1C) fills x 769–1120, y 2146–2311 px. That is the same box as the green Next (#81B64C, lip #5A7F35). Small actions that don't apply are greyed out, not removed: Best is greyed when your move was best, Show is greyed on an inaccuracy. So the small slots never move. Show turns into Hide in place and plays the engine line inside the bubble, highlighting the current move.

findings.claim: Before you solve a puzzle in the app (classic, rating-focused mode), the screen shows a white 'White to Move' card above the board, the rating plus a timer and a small rating graph below it, and a three-slot bottom bar: Hint on the left, Back in the middle, and a greyed-out Next on the right.
findings.detail: VERIFIED and measured: nav bar 58 pt (back arrow, orange puzzle icon with 'Puzzles' title, cog). An empty prompt zone 182 pt tall, with the white card (45 pt tall, side-coloured square plus bold 'White to Move') sitting at its bottom-left, 29 pt above the board. The board is 390 pt and edge to edge. The area below it is 181 pt. Bottom-bar items are centred at about 15%, 49% and 85% of the screen width. The board's top edge is about 240 pt below the top of the nav bar.

findings.claim: After a correct solve in points mode, the prompt card is swapped in place for a result card ('✓ ♛xc1# is correct!' in green). Below the board you see the score with '+42', a streak flame ('2 in a row'), a timer and a yellow progress bar. The bottom bar becomes Analysis on the left, a large green 'Next' (arrow icon) in the middle, and Retry on the right.
findings.detail: VERIFIED and measured on Android (1080 px = 360 dp): result card 47 dp tall and 13 dp above the board; Next 167×54 dp (46% of width); progress bar 14 dp thick; 75 dp gap from board to Next. The App Store mock shows the same: Next is 47.6% of screen width, with the side items centred at 12% and 88%. A correct move also gets a green check badge on the corner of its square (iPad App Store screenshot; web Help Center screenshot).

findings.claim: Chess.com added a delay of about 3 seconds before the puzzle Hint button works, because people were hitting Hint by accident right after tapping Next. Users said the real problem was that Hint appeared where a different button had just been, and that it sat too close to Retry.
findings.detail: VERIFIED quotes. DeepGreene, Aug 22, 2022: 'some puzzlers were accidentally hitting Hint immediately after hitting Next'; 'it might be three' seconds. Iris_for_the_Pin (Android): 'this frequently causes me to hit Hint, too, after I've hit retry.' AndersonConnors: 'the button shouldn't appear in the exact same place that a different button used to be... The delay doesn't solve this.' Lichess does the same thing in code: Hint and 'View the solution' stay disabled for 4 s after a puzzle loads. Whether Chess.com still has the delay in 2026 is not confirmed.

findings.claim: The Aug 2024 mobile puzzle redesign was criticised for the coach and its bubble taking up to half the screen, a smaller board pushed toward the bottom, a 'giant red retry button', Hint at the bottom-left, a rating graph too small to read, and an always-on 'White to move' bubble. A Chess.com-linked forum regular, Martin_Stahl (not labelled as staff), said the redesign was meant to 'de-emphasize rating', and that an iOS update temporarily removed the coach.
findings.detail: VERIFIED quotes, Aug–Sep 2024: 'takes up half the phone screen', 'Board not in the center but shifted towards the bottom', 'I keep clicking the wrong places coz the layout is unintuitive', 'Everything is smaller now in the puzzle UI on the mobile app.' Daily Puzzle Android, Dec 2025: a large white bubble above the board clips the tops of 3D pieces (https://www.chess.com/forum/view/site-feedback/daily-puzzle-ui).

findings.claim: On mobile, tap-to-move and drag both work all the time, and the iOS app has no setting to turn dragging off. Users keep complaining that this causes accidental moves, through November 2026.
findings.detail: VERIFIED. Help Center: 'On mobile, you can use both at any time.' Forum, Apr 2024: 'I literally never do it intentionally and have had it cost me a few games.' App Store review, Nov 7, 2026 (3 stars, v4.10.37): 'The app needs a way to turn off dragging pieces. It accomplishes nothing but forcing random misclicks.' Sep 2025 review: 'I think I'm placing a piece one place, it lands one short or one past.'

findings.claim: Whether the Chess.com app enlarges or lifts a piece while you drag it could NOT be confirmed. The iOS Board settings have no magnify option. Lichess's open-source app does both by default: the dragged piece is drawn at 2× size, one square above your finger, with a shaded circle two squares wide marking the target square.
findings.detail: Chess.com: UNVERIFIED. App Store marketing art shows an enlarged piece on a raised yellow tile with a drop shadow, but that is an illustration, not the drag behaviour. Lichess: VERIFIED in code: magnifyDraggedPiece=true sets dragFeedbackScale 2.0 and dragFeedbackOffset (0, −1 square). dragTargetKind=circle draws a circle with radius one square, filled 0x33000000 (20% black). A drag starts after 3 px of movement. Move method can be Either / Tap two squares / Drag.

findings.claim: iOS Board settings are: Phonetic Alphabet, Sounds, Haptic Feedback, Show Coordinates, Highlight Last Move, Show Legal Moves, Faster Animation, and Castling Method (Normal). Piece-animation styles are Android-only. The board cannot be resized in the apps.
findings.detail: VERIFIED from the screenshot and article text. Rows are about 48 pt tall with iOS toggles. The last-move highlight shows as #F6F682 on light squares and #BBCA44 on dark squares (board #EEEED2 / #769656).

findings.claim: Haptics: 'Haptic Feedback' (Settings > Board) gives a slight vibration after every move, and 'Low-Time Haptic Feedback' (Play > Live Chess) buzzes when your clock is low. Users complain the move buzz comes after the move, also fires on the opponent's moves, and is too strong.
findings.detail: VERIFIED. golu91, Mar 2025: 'the vibration happens after the move is made, which feels unnatural'. They prefer Lichess beta's 'subtle vibration while I'm making my move'. SebLuRtZ, Nov 2025: 'too brutal... completely unusable on quick games <= 3min or when reviewing games'. Lichess code calls HapticFeedback.lightImpact when you jump to a move.

findings.claim: Live Chess settings on iOS: Confirm Each Move, Auto-Queen, Enable Premoves, Low-Time Sound Warning, Low-Time Haptic Feedback. Daily Chess settings: After I Move, Confirm Each Move, On Vacation. The Help Center says that with confirmation on, each move shows a checkbox to confirm, but what the confirm control actually looks like and where it sits were NOT confirmed.
findings.detail: Settings names VERIFIED. Confirm UI UNVERIFIED. App Store reviews from 2023 report moves submitting without confirmation and the opponent's clock running during the confirm step.

findings.claim: Resigning in a game: tap the first (≡) item in the bottom bar, choose Resign, then confirm with a checkmark. Earlier layouts caused accidental resigns because Resign and Draw sat near the move arrows, and the confirm pop-up appeared right on top of the arrows, so quick repeated taps confirmed it.
findings.detail: VERIFIED quotes. 2020: buttons 'very close to the arrow buttons'. Aug 2022, phone: the confirm 'popped up directly over the arrows'. 2021: 'the resign button is exactly under the back button'. In-game toolbar (App Store screenshot): 4 icon-only slots — ≡ (options), chat, ‹, ›. After the game a fifth, centre slot appears: a green 79×51 pt Game Review star button.

findings.claim: Move-quality icon colours, taken from Chess.com's own Help Center icon files: Brilliant #26C2A3 (!!), Great #749BBF (!), Best #81B64C (star), Excellent #81B64C (thumbs-up), Good #95B776 (check), Book #D5A47D (book), Inaccuracy #F7C631 (?!), Mistake #FFA459 (?), Miss #FF7769 (x), Blunder #FA412D (??).
findings.detail: VERIFIED by sampling pixels. On the board, the badge is a circle about 24 pt wide (about half a square) centred on the top-right corner of the destination square, with a white symbol. The same icon and coloured move text also appear inline in the move list. Thresholds in expected points lost: Best 0, Excellent ≤0.02, Good ≤0.05, Inaccuracy ≤0.10, Mistake ≤0.20, Blunder >0.20.

findings.claim: Coach arrows in Game Review: green = a better move or good option, red = threats or problems, orange = the main idea being explained, blue = the opponent's plans. Highlighted squares use the same colours. A separate green Best Move arrow appears depending on the 'Show Arrows' setting.

The Analysis screen on the app has a five-slot labelled bottom bar: Options, Game Review, Explore, Back, Forward on iOS (Android order: Options, Explorer, Game Review, Back, Forward). Two engine lines sit above the board, the full move list wraps as a paragraph below it, and Options opens a native action sheet (Reset, Flip Board, Share, Finish vs Bot).
findings.detail: VERIFIED and measured: each slot is about 78 pt wide; the bar is about 58 pt plus about 26 pt of home-indicator space (#1D1B1A). Back and Forward are the two rightmost slots. Action-sheet rows are about 57 pt, with a separate Cancel. Engine lines and Move Feedback can't be on at the same time. What the Explore/opening-explorer screen shows on mobile was not confirmed.

findings.claim: The July 2024 Game Review redesign moved the coach permanently to the top of the screen. Chess.com reported +25% Game Review usage and +20% subscription purchases. Mobile users complained about the one-row horizontal move list (about 5 moves visible), the bubble covering the eval bar, and having to tap the small arrows over and over.
findings.detail: Sep 2024 quotes: 'I have to click infinitely horizontally with the little arrows instead of easily scrolling through all my moves'; 'Side swiping for numerous moves is PITA'; 'Half the time the little speech bubbles cover the evaluation bar.'

findings.claim: Recent App Store reviews (2025–2026) back up mis-tap pain: a mis-tap on Retry auto-solved the Daily Puzzle, misclicks lose games, a Nov 2026 update made the board and text smaller, and move arrows were removed in bot games.
findings.detail: VERIFIED verbatim. Jun 2, 2026: 'i misclick the retry button and the board starts moving all on its own and instantly solves the daily puzzle... put the button in a harder to press spot, make it require 2 screen taps'. Nov 6, 2026: 'Board changed to too small'; 'New Game Look... Too small print'. Jan 2026: 'Buttons don't respond when they should, but somehow always respond when you don't want them to.' Oct 2025: 'you can no longer quickly click back and forward arrows... nowhere near as intuitive'. The play screen may have changed in v4.10.37 (Nov 3, 2026), after the screenshots used here were taken.

findings.claim: Daily Puzzle gives 5 hearts. A wrong move costs a heart and the coach gives a tip. Hard Mode hides the tips. A Share card shows your hearts. On the web, Hint first highlights the piece to move (teal square) with coach text, and the same button then turns into 'Move' to show the answer.
findings.detail: The step-by-step hint was VERIFIED in web screenshots. The mobile hint visuals were not seen.

findings.claim: App navigation: five bottom tabs (Home, Puzzles, Learn, Watch, More), about 58 pt plus safe area. Home keeps a full-width green 'Play' button pinned just above the tab bar. Learn shows a tile path with a square list button and a large green 'Next Lesson' button.
findings.source: App Store screenshots https://apps.apple.com/us/app/chess-play-learn/id329218549 and custom page ?ppid=f6295c2f-d9f1-4e5f-a40b-1155ec4139df ; Help Center screenshots
findings.detail: Some screenshots label the first tab 'Play' instead of 'Home', i.e. different versions.

findings.claim: Lessons: newer lessons are coach-guided exercises rather than videos, and some Lesson Library features aren't in the app. The in-app lesson challenge screen (hint, solution, feedback) was NOT confirmed. A 2024 review complains you can't step back through moves after lesson challenges.
findings.source: https://support.chess.com/en/articles/8609703-how-do-lessons-work-on-chess-com (updated Jul 13, 2026); App Store review Aug 6, 2024 (RSS feed)

findings.claim: Puzzle Rush offers 3-minute, 5-minute and Survival modes, and ends after three wrong puzzles. A missed puzzle shows a red X. The in-app layout during a run (where the strikes and timer sit) was NOT confirmed.
findings.detail: Web screenshot: Best Today and Top Score at the top, a stacked mode picker (3 min / 5 min / Survival, selected one with a green border), and a pinned green Play button.

findings.claim: The full Practice feature is web-only. The apps only have Drills, under More > Drills. Courses are web-only as of Sep 2026.
There is no sign that the app uses swiping on the board itself to step through moves. Swiping happens on the move list.
findings.detail: Based on absence of evidence: no Help Center or forum source mentions swiping on the board.

findings.claim: Reddit (r/chess, r/chessbeginners) could not be searched. WebFetch refuses reddit.com, and the available search index returned no Reddit results. Chess.com forums and the official App Store reviews feed were used instead.

patterns.name: Bottom action bar: one filled main button plus small icon-over-label buttons
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com Game Review, Puzzles (solved state), post-game bar
patterns.description: The bar sits directly above the home indicator (about 38 pt of safe area below it) and is about 56 pt tall. Game Review: three small buttons (Show, Best, Retry), each a 17–20 pt line icon over a label of about 13 pt, grey #909090 on #312E2B, centred at 48 / 128 / 208 pt (80 pt apart on a 390-pt screen). The main button is on the right: a 118×56 pt rounded rectangle (52 pt face #81B64C plus a 4 pt darker #5A7F35 bottom edge that looks like a key; corners about 10–12 pt; bold white label about 20 pt), 16 pt from the right edge. The visible gap between the last small label and the main button is about 35 pt. Puzzles (solved): Analysis on the left, Next in the centre (about 46–48% of the width, about 50–56 pt tall, arrow icon plus label), Retry on the right; the side items are centred at about 12% and 88% of the width. Post-game: five equal 78-pt slots, the centre one a 79×51 pt green button.
patterns.applyHere: The drill result row (src/routes/drill/+page.svelte, around lines 1107–1115) has three filled buttons with a 10 px gap (Try again / Why? / Continue at flex 1/1/1.6). Make Continue the only filled button: at least 52 pt tall, at least 45% of the width, pinned bottom-right or centre. Turn Try again and Why? into icon-over-label buttons in fixed equal slots, with 24–35 pt of empty space between them and Continue.

patterns.name: Fixed slots: grey out, don't remove
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com Game Review (Best greyed when your move was best; Show greyed on an inaccuracy)
patterns.description: Every small action keeps the same x position in every review state. Actions that don't apply are dimmed (about #606060 instead of #909090), not taken out, so nothing shifts sideways. The board's top edge and the bar stay at the same y across states (measured identical in all screenshots).
patterns.applyHere: Keep the drill's action-row layout identical whether you're answering, wrong, or seeing the result. Show disabled buttons instead of adding and removing them with {#if}, so buttons never shift under the thumb between taps.

patterns.name: Main button that changes job, with colour + label change and a tap guard
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com Game Review (Next ↔ Retry); Chess.com puzzle Hint delay of about 3 s; Lichess Hint/Solution disabled for 4 s
patterns.description: After an inaccuracy or mistake, the same 118×56 pt rectangle turns red #E02828 (edge #9D1C1C) and says 'Retry', while 'Next' moves down to a small slot (arrow icon plus label). Chess.com added an input delay of about 3 s on Hint because users hit it by accident right after Next (Hint appeared where Next had been). Lichess keeps Hint and 'View the solution' disabled for 4 s after a puzzle loads.
patterns.applyHere: Wherever a drill button changes meaning in place (Try again → Continue, or Show answer appearing where Try again was), ignore taps for about 400–600 ms after the change or require a fresh touch, and change both colour and label. Better still: never put a different action under the spot the user just tapped.

patterns.name: Fixed-height feedback zone above an edge-to-edge board
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com Game Review coach bubble; Puzzles prompt/result card
patterns.description: Nav bar 56–58 pt, then an optional 20 pt horizontal eval bar, then a fixed zone of about 160–182 pt, then the board (390×390 pt on a 390-pt phone, no side margins). The zone holds either the avatar (about 80 pt) with a white speech bubble (corners about 16 pt; headline = 24 pt class icon + bold verdict about 18 pt + dark eval chip on the right; body 1–3 lines of about 17 pt), or in puzzles a white card about 45–47 pt tall ('■ White to Move') that is replaced in place by '✓ ♛xc1# is correct!' in green. The card sits 10–29 pt above the board, so short messages leave empty space above and the board never moves. The bubble can be dragged down if it covers something.
patterns.applyHere: Reserve a fixed-height slot for the drill prompt and result, and swap the result into the prompt's box, so neither the board nor the buttons move when the answer is judged. Layout shift right after a tap is a classic cause of mis-taps.

patterns.name: Board-first space budget
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com Game Review, Analysis, Puzzles, games
patterns.description: The board spans the full width. Coordinates are drawn inside the edge squares (rank top-left, file bottom-right, about 11 pt), so no outer border is needed. The eval bar is horizontal at the top (setting 'Eval Bar Location: Top'), not beside the board. Two compact engine lines (about 27 pt each) go above the board. The move list is one horizontal row. Rarely used actions live behind ≡ / Options sheets, and settings open in sheets. Measured budget on a 390×844 phone: nav 56 + eval 20 + coach 162 + board 390 + move list and gaps 88 + actions 56 + safe area 38.
patterns.applyHere: Use the same vertical budget for the drill page on phones. Move lines, notes and long text into the Why sheet rather than stacking them between the board and the buttons.

patterns.name: Move list with edge chevrons and swipe; long-press repeat
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com Game Review move list; Lichess prev/next as bottom-bar buttons with auto-repeat
patterns.description: One row about 39 pt tall under the board. Chevron buttons sit at the far left and right with hit boxes of about 36×39 pt (the glyph itself is only about 5×14 pt). Moves are spaced about 15–25 pt apart. The current move sits in a pill about 24 pt tall (#413F3C with a 2 pt lighter bottom edge). Best moves show their icon and green text inline. You swipe the row sideways. Users dislike tapping the little arrows repeatedly. Lichess puts prev/next in a 56-pt bottom bar with press-and-hold repeat (500 → 250 → 100 ms) and a light haptic when jumping to a move.
patterns.applyHere: The drill move row (around lines 939–965; CSS around 1400–1460) uses 34×34 px icon buttons with 2 px gaps, and move pills with 4×6 px padding and 1 px gaps — exactly the cramped case. Space the pills at least 8–12 px apart and give them 36–44 px of tap height (keep the 24 px look using padding or a ::before hit area). Put the chevrons at the row ends with at least 44×44 px hit boxes, and add hold-to-repeat.

patterns.name: Bottom toolbar of five equal labelled slots, Back/Forward at the far right
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com Analysis (Options | Game Review | Explore | Back | Forward)
patterns.description: Each slot is about 78 pt wide and about 58 pt tall (plus about 26 pt of home-indicator space), with an icon of about 24 pt over a label of about 13 pt that is always visible, on #1D1B1A. Back and Forward are the two rightmost slots, where the right thumb rests. Options opens a native action sheet with rows of about 57 pt (Reset, Flip Board, Share, Finish vs Bot) and a separate Cancel.
patterns.applyHere: In the Why sheet (around lines 1155–1180), the chevrons are 20 px icons next to the Play pill. Try a bottom toolbar inside the sheet with Back and Forward as wide labelled slots on the right and Play in the centre.

patterns.name: Result badge on the square
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com Game Review, Puzzles, end-of-game glyphs
patterns.description: A circle about 24 pt wide (about 50% of a 48.75 pt square), centred on the top-right corner of the destination square, with a white symbol. Colours: Brilliant #26C2A3, Great #749BBF, Best/Excellent #81B64C, Good #95B776, Book #D5A47D, Inaccuracy #F7C631, Mistake #FFA459, Miss #FF7769, Blunder #FA412D. Puzzles use the same geometry: a green check for correct, a red X for misses. End of game: a crown on the winner's king, a flag on the loser's (on time). Last-move highlight: #F6F682 on light squares, #BBCA44 on dark.
patterns.applyHere: Show the drill verdict as a badge on the square of the move just played, plus a single short headline. The eye is already there, so it does the job of a separate result line.

patterns.name: Hint that escalates in place
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com Daily Puzzle (web); Lichess puzzle hint square; Chess.com Game Review Retry with optional hint
patterns.description: The first tap highlights the piece to move (teal square) and the coach asks a guiding question. The same button then turns into 'Move' to show the answer. Lichess highlights the hint square and keeps the Hint button highlighted while it's active.
patterns.applyHere: Replace the drill's separate 'show it' / 'Show answer' controls with one Hint button that escalates (piece → square → move). Revealing the answer then takes deliberate taps on a button that is not next to Try again.

patterns.name: Irreversible actions kept away from navigation and confirmed elsewhere
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com Resign in the ≡ menu with confirm; documented failures in analysis mode and Daily Puzzle
patterns.description: Resign is reached through the first (≡) toolbar item, then confirmed with a checkmark. Recorded failures: Resign and Draw near the move arrows, the confirm pop-up landing on top of the arrows so quick taps confirmed it, and a 2026 review where a mis-tap on Retry auto-solved the Daily Puzzle ('require 2 screen taps').
patterns.applyHere: Take 'Show answer' and 'I play X on purpose · stop drilling this' (around lines 1093–1103) out of the main action row. Put them in an overflow menu, or require press-and-hold or a second tap. Never place a confirm control where the finger already is.

patterns.name: Forgiving touch input: drag threshold, magnified dragged piece, target circle, tap-only option
patterns.seenIn: Lichess mobile (open source); Chess.com's lack of a tap-only toggle drives complaints
patterns.description: Lichess offers move method Either / Tap / Drag. The dragged piece is drawn at 2× square size and one square above the finger. The target square is shown by a circle with a radius of one square, filled 20% black. A drag only starts after 3 px of movement, and the default animation is 250 ms. Chess.com accepts tap and drag at all times and users ask for a toggle.
patterns.applyHere: If the drill board's touch handling is custom, add the magnified, lifted dragged piece and the target circle, and offer a tap-only setting for people who drag by accident.

patterns.name: Light, immediate haptics only for your own action
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com 'Haptic Feedback' after every move (criticised); Lichess light impact
patterns.description: Chess.com's buzz after each move fires late and also on the opponent's moves. Users call it 'brutal' and ask for a subtle, keyboard-like tick during the touch.
patterns.applyHere: The repo already ticks during the touch on iPhone (commit a2229a1). Keep it to one light tick when the user commits, and don't vibrate on auto-played replies or repeated navigation steps.

patterns.name: Full-width main call-to-action pinned above the tab bar
patterns.seenIn: Chess.com Home 'Play', Learn 'Next Lesson', Game Review 'Start Review', Play Coach 'Play'
patterns.description: A full-width green button (12–16 pt side margins, about 54–56 pt tall, 3D bottom edge) pinned just above the 5-tab bar or the home indicator. Secondary options scroll in the content above it. Learn puts a square list button (about 56 pt) to the left of it.
patterns.applyHere: On the drill's empty and finished screens, pin one full-width 'Go again' at the bottom, and make 'Done' a quiet text button well away from it rather than an equal button next to it.

lichess-trainers.topic: How Lichess mobile (Flutter source, plus lichess.org mobile web), mobile opening and drill trainers, and learning apps (Duolingo, Anki, Brilliant, Khan) lay out answer, feedback and next controls so there is one primary action within thumb reach and adjacent mis-taps are rare. Includes concrete sizes and timings from source code.

findings.claim: Lichess's shared BottomBar on Android and on iOS before 26 is 56pt tall plus the bottom safe area. It has 8pt horizontal and 4pt vertical padding. Every button is wrapped in Expanded, so the buttons are equal-width cells, each with a full-cell hit area about 48pt tall. Grouped buttons are flattened into normal cells, and text scaling inside the bar is capped at 1.4x.
findings.detail: BottomAppBar(height: kBottomBarHeight=56, padding: EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 8, vertical: 4)), children: ungrouped.map((c) => Expanded(child: c)). Each BottomBarButton is an InkWell filling its cell (L606). With 4 buttons on a 390pt-wide iPhone, each cell is about 93x48pt; with 5 buttons it is about 75x48pt.

findings.claim: BottomBarButton shows only an icon by default (showLabel=false). The label appears in a long-press tooltip and in accessibility semantics. A disabled button is drawn at 40% opacity with a null onTap. 'highlighted' tints the icon with the primary color. 'blink' pulses a 20%-primary background on a 2000ms cycle to say 'tap me next'.
findings.detail: Labels are switched on (showLabel: true) only where the action is not obvious: explorer DB/Prev/Next, the retro 'View the solution' / 'Skip this move' / 'Next mistake', and gamebook 'Next' / 'Retry'. Icon size is the Flutter default of 24.

findings.claim: On iOS 26 (liquid glass), the bar becomes floating capsules: 48pt tall, 24pt icons, at least 8pt between capsules, evenly spaced. Icon-only buttons are 48pt circles. Labeled capsules have 16pt side padding and 15pt/w500 text. Related buttons, such as Prev/Next, share one capsule with 48pt-wide slots. The bar has 8pt above it and dips 8pt into the home-indicator inset (bottom padding = safe inset - 8, minimum 8).
findings.detail: _kGlassCapsuleHeight=48, _kGlassIconSize=24, _minSpacing=8, _kGlassBarTopPadding=8, _kGlassBarSafeAreaOverlap=8. When capsules don't fit, the widest ones shrink first. The main action can be marked 'prominent' (tinted capsule). A blinking button is rendered as prominent.

findings.claim: Lichess keeps each bottom bar to 2-5 targets and moves everything else into a Menu action sheet.
findings.detail: Puzzle while solving: Hint, View solution, Prev, Next. Puzzle when solved: Menu, Analysis, Continue training (highlighted), Prev, Next; the Menu holds Flip / Share / View game. Analysis: Menu (+ small-board toggle), Engine, Prev, Next; settings, flip and share are all in the Menu sheet. Explorer: DB (labeled, opens a settings sheet), Flip, Prev, Next. Retro (learn from your mistakes) while solving: only 'View the solution' and 'Skip this move', both labeled; after a correct answer, Back/Next plus a blinking 'Next mistake'. Practice gamebook: 'Play again' plus ONE slot that changes by state: View solution, then Next, Retry or Next chapter.

findings.claim: Lichess delays the hint and solution buttons so they can't be hit by reflex. In the app, Hint and View solution stay disabled for 4s after each puzzle loads and once the line is finished. On lichess.org web they are hidden for 4000ms in rated puzzles and 2000ms in casual ones, then fade in over 1.5s (code comment: 'just to delay button display').

Lichess puzzle flow has no 'Try again' button. A wrong move shows 'That's not the move! / Try something else.' and is taken back automatically after 500ms (300ms on web), leaving the board live for another try. A right move shows 'Best move! / Keep going…' and the opponent's reply plays after 500ms. After 'View solution', the first solution move plays after 800ms and the Next arrow starts blinking.
findings.detail: There is an optional 'autoNext' (default false) that loads the next puzzle on success (puzzle_controller.dart#L350-L354). Learn-from-mistakes works the same way: incorrect shows 'You can do better / Try another move' and auto-retries, and the user's original mistake is drawn as a translucent red arrow (retro_screen.dart#L226-L240).

findings.claim: Lichess shows feedback as a compact tile: a 36pt colored check or cross (or a 48pt king on a 50pt board-colored square for 'Your turn'), a bold title at 1.2x body size, and a subtitle of up to 2 lines. In a portrait puzzle the tile sits ABOVE the board; rating and session sit below it, then the bar. In retro mode the tile is centered under the board, above the floating bar.
findings.detail: The copy pattern is a 2-3 word verdict plus one instruction ('Best move!' / 'Keep going…'; 'That's not the move!' / 'Try something else.'; 'Success!' / 'Puzzle complete!'). Feedback text is never placed inside the button row.

findings.claim: Prev/Next in Lichess are RepeatButtons: a long press steps repeatedly with acceleration. Puzzles use 500ms, 250ms, 100ms, then every 30ms. The default schedule is 200, 180, 100, 40ms, then 30ms. A selectionClick haptic fires when repeating starts.

Lichess uses haptics sparingly. Moves and captures get lightImpact and checks get mediumImpact, behind a 'Touch feedback' setting that defaults to on. Other uses: selectionClick when hold-to-repeat starts, mediumImpact on context menus, lightImpact on pull-to-refresh and when replaying moves in a game, heavyImpact on a Puzzle Storm wrong move and on combo level-up. Regular puzzles play no extra success or failure haptic or sound beyond the move itself; only Streak and Storm play error and confirmation sounds.

Lichess board-input defaults for touch: tap OR drag is allowed. 'Magnify dragged piece' is on: the dragged piece is drawn at 2x and lifted one square above the finger. The drop target under the finger is a circle twice the size of a square. 'Move on release' is off (when on, tap-to-move commits on lift so you can slide to change the destination). Piece animation is 150ms.
findings.detail: dragFeedbackScale: 2.0, dragFeedbackOffset: Offset(0, -1). The math is ((dy-1)*feedbackSize)/2, so the piece's center ends up 1 square above the touch point. Setting copy: 'When moving a piece by tapping, the move is made when you lift your finger, letting you slide to change the destination square.' The web chessground v9 used by this app has no magnify or offset option: the dragged piece sits centered under the thumb.

findings.claim: Lichess shape drawing on touch uses two fingers: hold one finger on an empty square and drag a second finger. Double-tapping an empty square within 200ms clears the shapes, and selecting a movable piece also clears them. Drawing defaults to on, in green.

Lichess keeps the board away from screen edges. Analysis-type screens inset the board 12pt (32pt on short screens). On iOS the board also claims touches in the 20pt back-swipe strip beside it, so dragging a/h-file pieces doesn't pop the screen. Users asked for a smaller board partly to avoid accidental back-swipes (issue #2849); there is now a 0.7x small-board toggle in the bar.

Lichess issue #1577 is exactly the user's problem. People tapping Next quickly at the bottom 'accidentally jumped forward' by hitting the move list just above the bar, usually on the 2nd or 3rd quick tap. The maintainer refused to move the buttons under the board (it would cost move-list space). A user suggested ignoring move-list taps for about 200ms after a forward/back tap. It was not implemented.
findings.detail: Quote (tom-anders): 'If the user has tapped the forward/backward button in the last 200ms, block tap events of the move list?' The drill page in this app has the same geometry: ◀ ▶ are 34x34px with a 2px gap to move buttons padded 4x6px (/Users/jwahbeh/chess-trainer/web/src/routes/drill/+page.svelte, .navrow/.mv CSS around L1400-L1460).

findings.claim: In Lichess, the move list and the explorer are secondary, passive targets. The inline move list is a 40pt-high horizontal scroller with items padded 3x4pt; it auto-centers the current move (alignment 0.5, 200ms ease-in, 100ms debounce). The PGN tree uses 16pt text with 1.5 line height and 6x2pt padding per move; long-pressing a move opens a bottom-sheet context menu. Explorer rows are about 40pt tall (10pt vertical padding), and every cell in a row plays the same move.
findings.detail: Counterexample: the analysis tab bar uses 18pt icons in 26pt-tall tabs (analysis_layout.dart#L437-L456), and puzzle session chips are 38x26 with 8pt spacing (puzzle_session_widget.dart#L81-L156). Lichess keeps these out of the hot path.

findings.claim: lichess.org mobile web (the closest analogue to a PWA) stacks board, then a controls row, then feedback/tools, then session. The controls row is 5rem (80px) tall on phones vs 3rem on desktop. Mobile analysis control buttons are flex:1 with min-height 3em; in the jump row, the first/last buttons are double width. touch-action is pan-y. After a solve, 'Continue training' is a full-width primary block with 2em padding and 1.3em text.

Chess.com staff confirmed that the puzzle Hint button got a delay because 'some puzzlers were accidentally hitting Hint immediately after hitting Next'. The delay is about 2-3s, and staff noted it is pointless on Retry. This is evidence that a control which appears where the finger just tapped gets hit by accident.

Chess.com's Game Review in the app: a green 'Next' button sits in the bottom-right corner. Show / Best / Retry options are along the bottom. The coach bubble updates each move and can be dragged down if it covers options. Arrows sit on either side of the move list below the board, and swiping the move list steps through moves. A later redesign put the Coach 'always at the top of the screen'.
findings.detail: Chess.com also offers 'Confirm Move' to 'avoid accidental taps', and on mobile tap and drag are always both enabled (https://support.chess.com/en/articles/8609803-how-do-i-turn-on-confirm-move ; https://support.chess.com/en/articles/8708726-how-do-i-make-moves-in-live-chess). Practice (formerly Drills) is not fully on mobile (https://support.chess.com/en/articles/8724749-what-is-practice-on-chess-com). Mobile Lessons layout is not documented publicly.

findings.claim: Chessable MoveTrainer: after a miss, 'you are shown the correct move once again instead and the quiz restarts'. Learn mode shows the line first; Review mode shows the answer only after a fail. Options include Reps (default 3), Time (default 60s) and Soft fail. One reviewer called the default playback speed 'way too slow'; another called the delays while showing the correct line 'quite annoying'.
findings.detail: I could not find a public description of the button layout on Chessable's mobile training screen.

findings.claim: Chessbook practice replays the line from the start, then asks for your move. You can ask for a hint or leave practice. Wrong moves come back soon, scheduled per move rather than per line. A valid alternative move isn't counted as a failure: the app 'will just ask you to still play the main move'. The team says it worked to make the site 'work just as well on mobile', and it offers Chess.com/Lichess board themes for realism.

Listudy (open source): a wrong move is undone instantly with 'This move is not in the study, try again.' Hint arrows show by default until every move in the position has been played twice. Tapping large areas (title, sidebar, highlight box) turns hints on, and the 'Show hints for this move!' link has an enlarged hit area. There is an optional 3s pause at the end of a line before the board resets, and a deliberate delay before the computer replies ('instant play by the ai feels weird').

Lotus Chess (iOS/Android, 4.8 stars from 1.1K ratings) builds an opening course from your Chess.com/Lichess games, which is the same idea as this app. It drills with the prompt 'Make the move you learned'. Reviews complain there is no explanation of why and no view of the line that led to a flashcard position; the developer agreed this needs work.
findings.detail: Store pages don't describe the button layout of the training screen.

findings.claim: AnkiMobile: tap anywhere on the card to reveal the answer; the bottom area then shows 2-4 answer buttons with the next interval above each. By default on the answer side, tapping the left side means Again (red) and the right side means Good (green); 'Taps near the middle of the screen will be ignored.' 'Double Tap Prevention … ignores a second tap when two taps are made in quick succession, so that you don't accidentally reveal the answer or advance to the next card.' Shaking the device undoes, optional ticks flash a check or cross top-right, and the bottom bar can be hidden.
findings.detail: In an Anki forum thread, a one-handed user on a 6.6-inch phone found Again 'uncomfortable to press … with just the right hand' and asked for left/right button placement. Some find gestures imprecise (https://forums.ankiweb.net/t/one-handed-mode/60548).

findings.claim: Duolingo: Check sits 'at the very bottom'. After checking, a result banner appears with the Continue/Next button. An open-source replica shows a full-width Check (the Skip button is hidden on phones), gray and disabled until an answer is picked, then green with a 4px darker bottom lip. A fixed bottom sheet then slides up: light-green background with green 'Good job!', or light-red with 'Correct solution:' plus the answer. A full-width Continue in the matching color takes the same bottom spot.
findings.detail: The replica and the design write-ups are unofficial. Blakecrosley describes the incorrect sheet sliding up over 200ms, a 'GOT IT' label on the wrong-answer button, and button specs of a 4px bottom lip and 16px radius; tastekit lists 50px height and 12px radius (https://tastekit.dev/gallery/apps/duolingo).

findings.claim: Duolingo puts small secondary controls inside the feedback sheet, away from Continue: 'after checking your answer in an exercise, you can hit the "Report" flag that appears next to the solution.' One accessibility critique measured the red and green feedback boxes at only 3.6:1 and 2.7:1 contrast, said the two look 'almost identical' to someone with deuteranomaly, and recommended adding icons.

Brilliant: 'When your answer is correct, the box turns green with a checkmark', and a 'Start over' button sits beneath the problem. Khan Academy marks the wrong option and shows a 'Not quite' panel with retry, help and skip. KA users have asked for an 'Are you sure you want to use a hint?' confirmation because learners hit Hint by accident.
findings.detail: For the KA hint request I only saw the post title; the help center blocks automated fetches. The screensdesign article warns: don't rely on red/green alone; 'a small error banner may be easy to miss if the primary action immediately encourages continuation'; the primary action 'should not cover the selected answer'.

findings.claim: Apple HIG: the default iOS control size is 44x44pt (minimum 28x28pt). 'Consider spacing between controls as important as size … add about 12 points of padding around elements that include a bezel. For elements without a bezel, about 24 points of padding works well.' It also says to pair audio cues with haptics.

Hoober's touch research: accuracy ranges from about 7mm at the center of the screen to 12mm at the corners. Dense content is fine mid-screen, but 'top and bottom action strips should hold very few items'. More than 4 items on an iOS bar (5 on the largest phones) invites trouble. Keep unrecoverable actions away from other controls. Users prefer to tap the center when given the choice.
findings.detail: Human Standards turns Hoober's figures into location minimums: top 11mm (31pt), center 7mm (20pt), bottom 12mm (34pt / 46px). It also recommends at least an 8px gap, ideally 8-12px, between adjacent targets.

findings.claim: ChessTempo's opening trainer could not be checked: chesstempo.com and its manual returned 403 or unextractable PDF text.

patterns.name: One primary slot that changes by state
patterns.description: A bottom-anchored primary button, full width or the larger 2/3 cell, at least 48-56pt tall, sitting just above env(safe-area-inset-bottom). Its label and color follow the state: Check → Continue (Duolingo); View solution → Next / Retry / Next chapter (Lichess practice gamebook, where the bar has only 2 cells); Show answer → answer buttons in the same bottom area (Anki). There is never more than one equal-weight neighbor. Feedback text sits above the button, not beside it.

patterns.applyHere: Today the drill footer (/Users/jwahbeh/chess-trainer/web/src/routes/drill/+page.svelte L1092-L1116) puts up to three 44px buttons side by side: Try again / Show answer, or Try again / Why? / Continue. Change it to: result → Continue as the single large primary (2/3 width, right side, ≥52px tall) with Why? as one smaller secondary cell on the far left. Wrong → no Try again button at all (see the auto-retry pattern below), with Show answer as the lone secondary cell. Keep at least 24px between the two cells, per HIG non-bezeled padding.

patterns.name: Tap guard when a button changes meaning
patterns.description: After a control appears or changes meaning under the thumb, ignore taps on it for a short time, and fade it in so the change is visible. Anki ignores a second quick tap so it doesn't reveal or advance by accident. Chess.com delays Hint by 2-3s because people hit it right after Next. Lichess keeps Hint/View solution off for 4s (web: 4s rated / 2s casual, 1.5s fade). Lichess issue #1577 proposes ignoring move-list taps for 200ms after a Prev/Next tap.

patterns.applyHere: When phase becomes 'result', or the footer swaps Try again ↔ Continue, set pointer-events:none on the new footer buttons for about 400ms and animate opacity from 0.4 to 1. Keep 'Show answer' / 'show it' disabled for about 2-3s after the question appears. After any ◀/▶ tap, ignore clicks on .moves and .chips for about 250ms (record a timestamp and return early in goTo/preview).

patterns.name: Prev/Next as big equal cells in a bottom bar
patterns.description: Navigation arrows live in a sticky bottom bar of 3-5 equal-width cells. Each cell is the full bar height (Lichess: 56pt bar → ~48pt cells, ~93pt wide with 4 buttons on a 390pt phone; iOS glass: 48pt capsules at least 8pt apart, with Prev/Next sharing one 2x48pt capsule). lichess.org mobile web uses an 80px controls row and min-height 3em buttons, with first/last double width. Scrubbing targets such as the move list are kept passive and away from the arrows.

patterns.name: Hold to fast-step
patterns.description: Long-pressing Prev/Next repeats with acceleration so users don't hammer the button (hammering is what causes neighbor mis-taps in #1577). Lichess puzzles use 500 → 250 → 100ms, then every 30ms (default 200/180/100/40 then 30ms), with a selectionClick haptic when repeating starts. The click that ends a long press does not count as an extra step.

patterns.applyHere: In the drill page, start a timer on pointerdown on ◀/▶ that calls step(±1) on the 500/250/100/30ms schedule, clear it on pointerup/cancel/leave, and swallow the click after a long press. Fire the existing tick from /Users/jwahbeh/chess-trainer/web/src/lib/haptics.ts at the start; it works on iPhone because pointerdown is inside the touch.

patterns.name: Auto-retry: take a wrong move back instead of showing a Try again button
patterns.description: A wrong move shows a short verdict ('That's not the move! / Try something else.'), and the board takes the move back after 300-500ms and stays live. The retry is the user's next move, so there is no retry button to hit. The only buttons left are secondary ones (Hint, View solution / Show answer). Learn-from-mistakes mode does the same and keeps the original mistake as a translucent red arrow. Listudy undoes immediately with 'This move is not in the study, try again.'

patterns.name: Fixed feedback zone, separate from the buttons

Chess.com moved the Coach to 'always at the top of the screen' and lets you drag the bubble out of the way. Duolingo keeps the message above Continue inside the sheet. Don't rely on red/green alone: add an icon and a text verdict.

patterns.name: Board drag ergonomics for thumbs

live.method:
I rendered the app live in system WebKit (Safari's engine) at iPhone size, not in Chrome. Playwright's Chrome would not start inside the command sandbox: Chrome aborts with FATAL "bootstrap_check_in com.google.Chrome.MachPortRendezvousServer: Permission denied", even with --single-process. Running it outside the sandbox was refused by the permission check, and `meta browser` couldn't reach its server. So I built a small WKWebView harness in Swift (/tmp/ux-probe/wk/browser.swift, binary /tmp/ux-probe/wk/hello) and drove it from Node through JSON command files (/tmp/ux-probe/wk.mjs, nav.mjs, measure.mjs, run-drill.mjs, run-pages.mjs).

Setup. Viewport 393x852 CSS px; innerWidth = clientWidth = 393, so no scrollbar gutter. User agent: iPhone iOS 18.6 Safari. navigator.standalone = true. Dark scheme. The page is visible (requestAnimationFrame runs at 62/s). DPR is 2. A script injected at document start forces :root{--safe-t:59px;--safe-b:34px} and hides scrollbars. Every safe-area use in the app goes through those two variables (app.css:31-32), so this emulates the Home Screen insets faithfully. No CSS uses display-mode; only InstallHint.svelte:7 checks it in JS, and that check also accepts navigator.standalone, so display-mode was not emulated.

Data. The setup link /?user=draco_jaco&period=3&reach=5 (lib/link.ts) imported 1,280 blitz games (Aug-Nov 2026) from the Chess.com API. The in-page analysis evaluated 628 positions (445 from the Lichess cloud cache, 183 by local Stockfish) and created 26 cards in under 15 s, well inside the time box. Storage was WebKit's in-memory data store.

Drill states. All result states use one card, opened with /drill?card=draco_jaco|white|6820108232337383|f1c4: Petrov's Defense as White, taught move 3.Nxe5, accepted alternative 3.d4, habit 3.Bc4 (played 5 times). I measured the deck-start "Your move" too; it was identical to drill-ask. The intro was skipped by tapping the board. Moves were made with real, trusted NSEvent clicks on from/to square centres computed from cg-board's rectangle, because chessground ignores untrusted events (drag.js:6). Buttons were pressed with element.click(). Before each measurement I waited until scrollHeight, target count and page text were unchanged for 3 s, since engine lines arrive asynchronously.

Measurement (in the page).
- Targets: outermost elements matching a[href], button, summary, input, select, textarea, label, [role=button], [tabindex]:not([tabindex=-1]), plus .cg-wrap counted as one target, "board".
- Rect: the border box clipped by scrolling ancestors and the viewport, in CSS px.
- A 5x5 elementFromPoint hit test drops covered elements (for example the 16 behind the Why sheet's backdrop).
- nearestGap: Euclidean edge-to-edge distance to the nearest other active target; 0 means touching or overlapping.
- Flags: under 44px in either dimension (unclipped box), and gap under 8px.
- Long pages list the targets on screen at scroll 0. Full-page lists in document coordinates are in /tmp/ux-probe/data/<state>.json under "page".

Screenshots, in /tmp/ux-probe/shots/:
- <state>.png at 1179x2556 (3x).
- <state>.annotated.png: boxes green = fine, orange = small or tight, red = both; each labelled WxH and gap; magenta stripes mark the safe areas.
- <state>.full.png for pages that scroll.

Cross-check against the real iPhone screenshot debug_photos/IMG_1390.PNG, sampling the pixel column at x=20:
- Eval-bar fill: y 108.3-115.7 on the device vs 108.7-115.7 in the harness.
- Board squares: 47.3px on the device vs 47.0-47.7px in the harness.
- Chip-row border: y 525-535 in both.

The repo was not modified; git status is the same as at the start.

live.limitations:
1) Engine: this is macOS WebKit (Safari's engine, SF Pro via -apple-system), not iOS Safari on a phone and not Chrome. Chrome could not start inside the sandbox, and permission to run it outside was denied. Layout and fonts should be very close to the iPhone, but small text-metric differences can change line wrapping. That matters, because the fit results depend on text: the note and the result box grow with their wording.

2) Pixel density: the harness runs at DPR 2, the phone at 3. chessground rounds the board to device pixels (render.js:159), so the inner board is 380px here and 378.67px on the iPhone (squares 47.5 vs 47.33px). The 381px wrapper, and everything below it, is the same at both densities. 1px borders are 2 device px here instead of 3.

3) Safe areas: emulated through the CSS variables at 59px top and 34px bottom. Other models report other insets. drill-correct fits with only 1.7px to spare (850.3 of 852), so even a couple of extra pixels of inset would make it scroll.

4) Input: clicks were mouse clicks (pointer: fine, hover: hover), not touch. The app's touch paths were not exercised (Board.svelte's touchstart/touchend handling, chessground's touch code, iOS tap behaviour). I parked the mouse in the top safe area before each screenshot to avoid :hover styling. Hit areas are border boxes. WebKit respects border-radius when hit-testing, so round and pill targets (Play, chips) are slightly smaller than their boxes (round Play: 84% of sample points hit). iOS adds no extra tap slop around elements.

5) Data: my profile differs from the user's phone. With 3 months and reach 5 it has 1,280 games and 26 cards; the phone shows 232 cards. With ?card= the counter reads 1/1. Text lengths (notes, result box, opening names) vary from card to card, so which states overflow will vary too; the result states were all measured on one card. The move row's contents and scroll position depend on the line being shown.

6) Snapshots: WebKit's snapshot doesn't render the tab bar's backdrop-filter blur, so the tab bar looks more see-through than on a device. Colours may be slightly shifted by colour-space conversion. In the .full.png images, fixed elements such as the tab bar appear once, at their scroll-0 position.

7) Gap flags on full-width list rows and on the tab bar are expected by design: those rows are 44px or taller and touch on purpose. They are not defects.

8) Thumb reach: nothing was tested with real hands; reach is inferred from y positions only.

9) States not measured: the intro replay, "Checking…", "You found it", cards played as Black, and landscape.

10) Clean-up: the harness used an in-memory data store. WebKit still created ~/Library/WebKit/hello and ~/Library/Caches/hello, which I removed. It also created three empty folders in $TMPDIR (com.apple.WebKit.{GPU,Networking,WebContent}+hello) that the sandbox would not let me delete; macOS clears $TMPDIR on its own. /tmp/ux-probe/profile is left over from the failed Chrome attempt. All scripts, data (/tmp/ux-probe/data/*.json, including the full-page "page" lists) and screenshots (/tmp/ux-probe/shots/) are in /tmp/ux-probe.
